title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
貴州鄉試錄序
隆慶庚午貴藩例當比士巡
按監察御史蔡廷臣司監臨
祇承
皇上求賢至意肅度矢公視故事
益嚴以紫徵淛等典試事淛
寡學竊聞貴本徼外西南夷
===
地靈淑之氣古猶盤鬱未舒
入
國朝始列版圖升爲藩司而解
額猶附於滇至嘉靖丁酉始
專科取士寔我
皇上虹流之歲則開
泰運於貴藩者已肇之矣今
punctuated:
貴州鄉試錄序

隆慶庚午，貴藩例當比士。巡按監察御史蔡廷臣司監臨，祇承皇上求賢至意，肅度矢公，視故事益嚴，以紫徵淛等典試事。淛寡學，竊聞貴本徼外西南夷地，靈淑之氣古猶盤鬱未舒。入國朝，始列版圖，升爲藩司，而解額猶附於滇。至嘉靖丁酉，始專科取士，寔我皇上虹流之歲，則開泰運於貴藩者已肇之矣。今
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guizhou Provincial Examination

In the gengwu year of Longqing (1570), Guizhou was due, according to established practice, to examine its scholars. Cai Tingchen, Regional Inspector serving as Investigating Censor, undertook supervision. Reverently carrying out His Majesty’s earnest intention to seek worthy men, he maintained solemn standards and pledged impartiality, applying greater rigor than customary precedent required. Zhe and others were commissioned to direct the examination [the wording 以紫徵 is doubtful; ?].

I, Zhe, though of scant learning, have heard that Guizhou was originally a land of the southwestern non-Han peoples beyond the frontier. In ancient times, its numinous and auspicious energies remained pent up, not yet unfolding. Only under our dynasty was it incorporated into the imperial territory and raised to the status of a province under a Provincial Administration Commission; even then, its quota of provincial graduates remained attached to Yunnan’s. Not until the dingyou year of Jiajing (1537) did it begin selecting scholars through a separate examination. That was indeed the year of His Majesty’s birth, marked by the auspicious flowing rainbow: the opening of an era of prosperity for Guizhou had thus already begun. Now …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
龍飛第二科澍濫竽校文其何以
須眞材仰稱
明詔於時御史率諸同事者奉
新政所須條格更相戒飭而後即
事合提學副使秦淦所選士
三試之遵
制額取三十人而不能盡錄者
===
多矣倚與盛哉何荒僻之地
人文殊尤凌邁至此哉夫人
才與氣運相流通而治化之
隆每徵於僻遠故唐虞聲教
所訖必曰朔南暨成周作人
以化及江漢爲候何者一元
幹旋自北而南其理不可誣
punctuated:
龍飛第二科，澍濫竽校文，其何以須眞材，仰稱明詔？於時，御史率諸同事者奉新政所須條格，更相戒飭而後即事。合提學副使秦淦所選士，三試之，遵制額取三十人，而不能盡錄者多矣。
倚與盛哉！何荒僻之地，人文殊尤凌邁至此哉？夫人才與氣運相流通，而治化之隆每徵於僻遠。故唐虞聲教所訖，必曰朔南；暨成周作人，以化及江漢爲候。何者？一元幹旋，自北而南，其理不可誣。
translation_en:
…the second examination since His Majesty ascended the throne. I, Shu, unworthily occupy a place among those judging the essays: how can I obtain true talent [?] and thereby fulfill the intent of the illustrious edict? At that time, the Censor led his colleagues in observing the regulations required by the new administration. They admonished one another before commencing their duties. They assembled the candidates selected by Qin Gan, Vice Commissioner for Education, and examined them in three sessions. In accordance with the prescribed quota, they selected thirty men, yet many others could not be included.
How flourishing indeed [?]! How could literary accomplishment in this remote and uncultivated land have attained such extraordinary distinction? Human talent and the fortunes of the age circulate together, and the flourishing of government and moral transformation is often evidenced in distant regions. Thus, accounts of the reach of the civilizing influence of Tang and Yu invariably speak of the north and south; when the Zhou dynasty nurtured men of talent, the extension of its transforming influence to the Jiang and Han rivers was taken as a sign of its achievement. Why is this? The primal cosmic force turns from north to south; this principle cannot be gainsaid…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
已貴雖逖界南服實與荆梁
鼎足而峙其山川聳拔濴洄
上薄青霄下瞰蛟室隱然有
圭璧之形金石之聲所以蘊
結而孕秀者蓋有待也我
太祖混一區宇養士育材二百年
來茲土漸濡
===
列聖洪潤盡變澆邪舊俗而絃誦
相聞渢渢乎與上國爭鳴又
仰荷
世宗特允專科亦旣寖明寖昌盛
倍往昔矣今
天子乘龍御極
南面聽天下開
punctuated: 已。貴雖逖界南服，實與荆梁鼎足而峙。其山川聳拔濴洄，上薄青霄，下瞰蛟室，隱然有圭璧之形、金石之聲，所以蘊結而孕秀者，蓋有待也。我太祖混一區宇，養士育材，二百年來，茲土漸濡列聖洪潤，盡變澆邪舊俗，而絃誦相聞，渢渢乎與上國爭鳴。又仰荷世宗特允專科，亦旣寖明寖昌，盛倍往昔矣。今天子乘龍御極，南面聽天下，開
translation_en:
…indeed. Although Guizhou lies far away on the southern frontier, it stands alongside Jing and Liang like the three legs of a tripod. Its mountains soar and its rivers swirl, reaching upward toward the azure heavens and overlooking the dwelling places of water dragons below. Within them lie the forms of jade tablets and disks and the sounds of bronze bells and stone chimes. The forces gathered there to nurture outstanding talent have surely been awaiting their time.

Our Taizu united the realm, fostered scholars, and cultivated talent. For two hundred years, this land has been steeped in the abundant beneficence of successive sage emperors. Its old customs of frivolity and perversity have been entirely transformed, and the sounds of strings and recitation can be heard everywhere, resounding richly in rivalry with the central regions. It further received from Shizong the special favor of authorization to hold its own examination. Learning has grown steadily brighter and more flourishing, its abundance now twice that of former times.

Now the Son of Heaven has mounted the dragon and ascended the throne. Facing south, he attends to the affairs of all under Heaven and inaugurates…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
經筵興禮樂尤
加意膠庠
採廷臣之議崇雅黜浮示天下以
還古炳炳乎觀聽一新即動
華顯承之際何以加焉宇內
時彥莫不響應景從願爲
帝臣矧貴士精采濯於
===
龍光意氣觸於感會有不歌忭
太和治化中以求自效乎渊幸
從執事之後慱觀其所爲文
類根極理道發揮仁義至於
析微顯權古今雖步驟錯綜
各以質䟽而溫潤雅馴粹然
一出於正是蓋
punctuated: 經筵，興禮樂，尤加意膠庠，採廷臣之議，崇雅黜浮，示天下以還古，炳炳乎觀聽一新。即動華顯承之際，何以加焉？宇內時彥，莫不響應景從，願爲帝臣。矧貴士精采濯於龍光，意氣觸於感會，有不歌忭太和治化中，以求自效乎？渊幸從執事之後，慱觀其所爲文，類根極理道，發揮仁義。至於析微顯、權古今，雖步驟錯綜，各以質䟽而溫潤，雅馴粹然，一出於正。是蓋
translation_en:
…the Classics Colloquium and promotes rites and music, giving particular attention to the schools. Adopting the proposals of his court officials, he honors refinement and rejects superficiality, showing all under Heaven the way back to antiquity. So brilliantly has he renewed what people see and hear! Even in the age of “Dong Hua’s illustrious succession” [?], how could this have been surpassed? Outstanding men throughout the realm respond like echoes and follow like shadows, wishing to serve as the Emperor’s ministers. How much more so the scholars of Guizhou, their spirits cleansed by imperial radiance and their aspirations stirred by this auspicious encounter! Could any fail to sing and rejoice amid the transforming governance of supreme harmony and seek to offer their service?
I, Yuan, have had the good fortune to follow behind those charged with conducting the examination and to read their compositions widely. These generally trace principle and the Way to their roots and expound benevolence and righteousness. In analyzing the subtle and the manifest and weighing past against present, their approaches, though varied and interwoven, each display an unadorned openness [?] together with warmth and polish. Refined, elegant, and pure, they proceed entirely from what is correct. This surely is…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
天啓我
明萬萬年無疆之昌祚將軼唐虞
成周而駕之肆發祥於遐陬
僻壤以副
皇上今日之用以昭
嚮明而治之盛固不止抒河嶽之
精英洩豐鎬之靈秀而已夫
===
楩楠杞梓木之良也然不產
於中原而木閣安籠諸箐山
所儲者爲有司采取貢之
天府足以棟
明堂而勝其任諸士受
昭代培植長養之澤如
高厚然今以言揚矣果克成其
punctuated:
天啓我明萬萬年無疆之昌祚，將軼唐虞、成周而駕之，肆發祥於遐陬僻壤，以副皇上今日之用，以昭嚮明而治之盛，固不止抒河嶽之精英、洩豐鎬之靈秀而已。
夫楩楠杞梓，木之良也，然不產於中原，而木閣、安籠諸箐山所儲者，爲有司采取，貢之天府，足以棟明堂而勝其任。諸士受昭代培植長養之澤，如高厚然，今以言揚矣，果克成其
translation_en:
…Heaven is opening for our Ming an auspicious destiny of boundless prosperity for myriad upon myriad years, which will surpass the ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the accomplished Zhou. Thus it brings forth auspicious signs in distant corners and remote places, supplying the men His Majesty needs today and displaying the flourishing rule of a sovereign who faces the light in governing. This assuredly does more than release the finest essences of rivers and mountains or reveal the numinous excellence of Feng and Hao.
Pian, nan, qi, and zi are fine timber trees. Yet they do not grow in the Central Plain; those held in the forested mountains of Muge and Anlong are harvested by the responsible officials and presented to the imperial treasury. They are fit to serve as ridgepoles for the Hall of Light and to bear that burden. You scholars have received the nurturing and sustaining bounty of this enlightened dynasty, as lofty as Heaven and as deep as Earth. Now you have been raised to prominence through your words. Can you indeed fulfill your…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
信勝
明堂之任爲貴士重耶〔制〕於是
諦思之忠信之資可以近道
爲其本質未漓振拔起爲易猶
之巨木有根由尋丈而蔽雲
霄未已也故虞舜大智不外
取深山野人言行以用其中
===
文王腹心亦得之兔罝武夫
蓋渾厚敦龐之士固
聖世所亟求也貴俗太朴未散士
多愿慤有受采受和之基兹
三十人者選自畎畝薦之
天廷不啻野人見取於虞舜而職
任所加行將有腹心之寄者
punctuated:
信，勝明堂之任，爲貴士重耶？〔制〕於是諦思之：忠信之資，可以近道，爲其本質未漓，振拔起爲易。猶之巨木有根，由尋丈而蔽雲霄，未已也。故虞舜大智，不外取深山野人言行，以用其中；文王腹心，亦得之兔罝武夫。蓋渾厚敦龐之士，固聖世所亟求也。
貴俗太朴未散，士多愿慤，有受采受和之基。兹三十人者，選自畎畝，薦之天廷，不啻野人見取於虞舜，而職任所加，行將有腹心之寄者
translation_en:
…fulfill their trust [?], bear the responsibilities of the Hall of Light, and bring distinction to the scholars of Guizhou? 〔Zhi [?]〕 Thereupon I considered this carefully: an endowment of loyalty and trustworthiness enables one to approach the Way. Because its underlying substance has not been diluted, it is easy to rouse and raise such men up. They resemble great trees with firm roots, growing from a few fathoms in height until they overshadow the clouds, without ceasing. Thus even the great wisdom of Shun of Yu consisted simply in drawing upon the words and deeds of rustic men from deep in the mountains and putting into practice what was balanced and fitting in them. King Wen likewise found his trusted confidants among the warriors described in “The Rabbit Net.” Men of substantial character, sincerity, and generosity are precisely those whom a sagely age urgently seeks.
The customs of Guizhou retain their original simplicity, and its scholars are mostly earnest and sincere. They possess the foundation upon which refinement and harmony may be imparted, as colors are applied to a suitable ground and flavors harmonized with a suitable base. These thirty men, selected from the fields and recommended to the imperial court, are no less fortunate than the rustic men whom Shun of Yu chose. As official duties are laid upon them, some will soon be entrusted with the responsibilities of intimate advisers…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
也非千載一時哉使諸士念
遭逢之不偶擴忠信之質爲
忠藎之思求善言善行無愧
野人初心而干城之具有以
克配武夫由之亮工熈載濟
濟師師以媲美唐虞成周勳
業則龍興致雲無負遭際之
盛而主司亦可幸以逭責矣
===
廼或靜言庸違不以堯舜文
武之道事吾
君卿
世宗之所以專科者何如
聖作之所以感召者何如而忍負
之耶制慶諸士類有所從故
punctuated:
也，非千載一時哉？使諸士念遭逢之不偶，擴忠信之質爲忠藎之思，求善言善行，無愧野人初心，而干城之具有以克配武夫。由之亮工熈載，濟濟師師，以媲美唐虞、成周勳業，則龍興致雲，無負遭際之盛，而主司亦可幸以逭責矣。
廼或靜言庸違，不以堯舜文武之道事吾君，卿世宗之所以專科者何如？聖作之所以感召者何如？而忍負之耶？制慶諸士類有所從，故
translation_en:
…Is this not an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years? Let these scholars reflect upon how exceptional their good fortune is, extend their innate loyalty and trustworthiness into a resolve of devoted service, and seek good words and good deeds, remaining true to their original aspirations as men of the countryside. Let their capacities as shields and walls of the state enable them fully to match those martial men. Through this, may they assist in accomplishing the work of government and bringing its undertakings to fruition, an imposing company serving as examples to one another, matching the achievements of the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and of the established Zhou dynasty. Then, as the dragon rises and draws the clouds to it, they will prove worthy of their splendid encounter with opportunity, and the officials presiding over the examination may also count themselves fortunate to escape blame.
But if any speak fine words in repose yet act contrary to them, failing to serve our sovereign according to the Way of Yao, Shun, King Wen, and King Wu, what then of Shizong’s purpose in establishing a separate examination [?]? What of the inspiration and response elicited by the sage sovereign’s actions? Could they bear to betray these? In congratulating these scholars [?], there is something for them to follow; therefore…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
於其始進也不厭忠告云是
舉也校士則〔渊〕與教諭陳〔彬〕
暨學正陳〔雲鵾〕教諭謝〔廷試〕
馬〔三才〕提調則左布政使蔡
〔文〕左叅議曹〔司賢〕監試則副
使程〔嗣功〕陸〔相儒〕先是巡撫
都御史王〔諍〕崇文振武風教
===
夙揚今都御史阮〔文中〕銜
命奠疆士心豫奮而左叅政王〔鳴〕
〔臣〕右叅政羅〔一道〕右叅議林
〔澄源〕楊〔祐〕副使李〔鳳〕僉事金
〔䑗〕防範於外綜理惟周若陞
任按察使劉〔炌〕右叅議樊〔做〕
贊襄始事與署都指揮僉事
punctuated: 於其始進也，不厭忠告云。是舉也，校士則〔渊〕與教諭陳〔彬〕暨學正陳〔雲鵾〕、教諭謝〔廷試〕、馬〔三才〕，提調則左布政使蔡〔文〕、左叅議曹〔司賢〕，監試則副使程〔嗣功〕、陸〔相儒〕。先是，巡撫都御史王〔諍〕崇文振武，風教夙揚。今都御史阮〔文中〕銜命奠疆，士心豫奮，而左叅政王〔鳴〕〔臣〕、右叅政羅〔一道〕、右叅議林〔澄源〕、楊〔祐〕、副使李〔鳳〕、僉事金〔䑗〕，防範於外，綜理惟周。若陞任按察使劉〔炌〕、右叅議樊〔做〕，贊襄始事，與署都指揮僉事
translation_en:
…at their initial entry into official life, I do not tire of offering loyal counsel.

For this examination, the examiners were I, Yuan, together with County School Instructor Chen Bin, Departmental School Instructor Chen Yunkun, and County School Instructors Xie Tingshi and Ma Sancai. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Cai Wen and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Cao Sixian. Overseeing the examination were Surveillance Vice Commissioners Cheng Sigong and Lu Xiangru.

Previously, Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Wang Zheng promoted civil learning and invigorated military affairs; his moral influence had long been manifest. Now Censor-in-Chief Ruan Wenzhong has received the imperial command to secure the frontier, and the scholars’ spirits are already uplifted. Left Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Mingchen, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Luo Yidao, Right Assistant Administration Commissioners Lin Chengyuan and Yang You, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Li Feng, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Jin Dang [?] maintained safeguards outside and managed the arrangements with thorough care. Liu Kai, promoted to Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Fan Zuo [?] assisted with the initial preparations, together with the Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
隆慶四年貴州鄉試
監臨官
巡按貴州監察御史蔡廷臣〔藎卿江西德化縣人乙丑進士〕
提調官
貴州等處承宣布政使司左布政使蔡文〔學中福建南靖縣籍龍溪縣人丁未進士〕
貴州等處承宣布政使司左參議曹司賢〔明卿湖廣武陵縣人庚戌進士〕
監試官
貴州等處提刑按察司副使程嗣功〔汝懋直隸歙縣人丁未進士〕
貴州等處提刑按察司副使陸相儒〔大衡浙江嘉興縣籍秀水縣人己未進士〕
===
考試官
直隸池州府儒學教授吳洌〔進之江西臨川縣人壬子貢士〕
江西饒州府餘干縣儒學教諭陳彬〔子斐福建惠安縣人丁酉貢士〕
同考試官
湖廣武昌府興國州儒學學正陳雲鵠〔子時廣西全州人甲子貢士〕
直隸鎮江府丹陽縣儒學教諭謝廷試〔爾一福建晉江縣人辛酉貢士〕
河南河南府孟津縣儒學教諭馬三才〔參卿雲南永昌衛籍應天府上元縣人辛酉貢士〕
印卷官
貴州等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷劉學博〔克一江西廬陵縣人監生〕
punctuated:
隆慶四年貴州鄉試。

監臨官。
巡按貴州監察御史蔡廷臣〔藎卿，江西德化縣人，乙丑進士〕。

提調官。
貴州等處承宣布政使司左布政使蔡文〔學中，福建南靖縣籍，龍溪縣人，丁未進士〕。
貴州等處承宣布政使司左參議曹司賢〔明卿，湖廣武陵縣人，庚戌進士〕。

監試官。
貴州等處提刑按察司副使程嗣功〔汝懋，直隸歙縣人，丁未進士〕。
貴州等處提刑按察司副使陸相儒〔大衡，浙江嘉興縣籍，秀水縣人，己未進士〕。

考試官。
直隸池州府儒學教授吳洌〔進之，江西臨川縣人，壬子貢士〕。

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子易事而難說也說之不以道不說也
及其使人也器之
好學近乎知力行近乎仁知恥近乎勇知
斯三者則知所以脩身
子路人告之以有過則喜禹聞善言則拜
大舜有大焉善與人同舍己從人樂取
於人以為善
===
易
君子體仁足以長人嘉會足以合禮利物
足以和義貞固足以幹事君子行此四
德者故曰乾元亨利貞
當位以節中正以通
言行君子之所以動天地也可不慎乎
聖人南面而聽天下嚮明而治
書
帝念哉德惟善政政在養民水火金木土
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

君子易事而難說也。說之不以道，不說也；及其使人也，器之。

好學近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇。知斯三者，則知所以脩身。

子路，人告之以有過則喜；禹聞善言則拜；大舜有大焉：善與人同，舍己從人，樂取於人以為善。

易

君子體仁，足以長人；嘉會，足以合禮；利物，足以和義；貞固，足以幹事。君子行此四德者，故曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」

當位以節，中正以通。

言行，君子之所以動天地也，可不慎乎？

聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治。

書

帝念哉！德惟善政，政在養民。水火金木土
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The gentleman is easy to serve but difficult to please. If one tries to please him in a way that does not accord with the Way, he is not pleased; when he employs people, he uses them according to their abilities.

To love learning is close to wisdom; to strive to put knowledge into practice is close to benevolence; to know shame is close to courage. Knowing these three, one knows how to cultivate oneself.

When someone told Zilu that he had a fault, he rejoiced. When Yu heard good counsel, he bowed. The great Shun surpassed even these: he shared with others in doing good, set aside his own views to follow others, and delighted in drawing upon others to do good.

Book of Changes

The gentleman embodies benevolence and is thus able to lead others; he brings together what is excellent and is thus able to accord with ritual propriety; he benefits things and is thus able to harmonize righteousness; he is steadfast and firm and is thus able to manage affairs. The gentleman practices these four virtues. Hence it is said: “Qian: primal greatness, success, benefit, and constancy.”

Occupying the proper position, he exercises restraint; being central and correct, he achieves free passage.

Words and deeds are the means by which the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth. Can he fail to be cautious?

The sage faces south and hears the affairs of all under Heaven; he turns toward the light and governs.

Book of Documents

O Emperor, give heed! Virtue consists in good government, and government lies in nourishing the people. Water, fire, metal, wood, earth…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
穀惟脩正德利用厚生惟和九功惟敘
九敘惟歌戒之用休董之用威勸之以
九歌俾勿壞
各守爾典以承天休
元后作民父母
學古入官議事以制政乃不迷其爾典常
作之師
詩
駉駉是中騧驪是騵
===
以祈甘雨以介我稷黍以穀我士女
帝謂文王予懷明德不大聲以色不長夏
以革不識不知順帝之則
昔有成湯自彼氐羌莫敢不來享莫敢不
來王曰商是常
春秋
冬鄭公孫夏帥師伐陳襄公二十有五年
叔孫豹會晉趙武楚公子圍齊國弱宋
向戌衛齊惡陳公子招蔡公孫歸生鄭
punctuated:
穀惟脩；正德、利用、厚生惟和。九功惟敘，九敘惟歌。戒之用休，董之用威，勸之以九歌，俾勿壞。
各守爾典，以承天休。
元后作民父母。
學古入官，議事以制，政乃不迷，其爾典常。
作之師。
詩
駉駉是中，騧驪是騵。
以祈甘雨，以介我稷黍，以穀我士女。
帝謂文王：「予懷明德，不大聲以色，不長夏以革，不識不知，順帝之則。」
昔有成湯，自彼氐羌，莫敢不來享，莫敢不來王，曰商是常。
春秋
冬，鄭公孫夏帥師伐陳。襄公二十有五年。
叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衛齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭
translation_en:
…grain are to be properly managed; rectifying virtue, promoting useful resources, and enriching livelihoods are to be brought into harmony. These nine achievements are to be duly ordered, and their ordering celebrated in song. Admonish them with blessings, supervise them with awe, and encourage them with the nine songs, so that these achievements do not fall into decay.

Let each of you observe your prescribed duties, thereby receiving Heaven’s blessings.

The sovereign acts as father and mother to the people.

Study antiquity before entering office; deliberate on affairs according to established rules. Then government will not go astray. Make these your constant standards.

Act as their teacher.

Book of Odes

Amid the spacious pastures [?] are buckskin horses, black horses, and chestnut horses with white bellies.

To pray for timely rain, to aid our millet crops, and to nourish our men and women.

The Lord on High said to King Wen: “I cherish your luminous virtue: without loud voices or imposing appearances, without extravagance or change, without conscious contrivance or calculation, you follow the rules of the Lord on High.”

Of old there was Cheng Tang. Even from among those Di and Qiang, none dared fail to come with offerings, none dared fail to come to acknowledge his kingship. They said, “Shang is the enduring rule.”

Spring and Autumn Annals

In winter, Gongsun Xia of Zheng led an army to attack Chen. The twenty-fifth year of Duke Xiang.

Shusun Bao met with Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, and, from Zheng, …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
罕虎許人曹人于虢〔昭公元年〕
秋齊侯宋公江人黄人會于陽穀〔僖公三
年〕
秋晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕
齊人歸我濟西田〔宣公十年〕齊人來歸鄆
讙龜陰田〔定公十年〕
禮記
一道德以同俗
以四時爲柄故事可勸也以日星爲紀故
===
事可列也月以爲量故功有藝也
是故先王慎所以感之者故禮以道其志
樂以和其聲政以一其行刑以防其姦
禮樂刑政其極一也所以同民心而出
治道也
儒有今人與居古人與稽今世行之後世
以爲楷
第貳場
論
punctuated:
罕虎、許人、曹人于虢〔昭公元年〕。
秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黄人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕。
秋，晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕。
齊人歸我濟西田〔宣公十年〕。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田〔定公十年〕。
禮記
一道德以同俗。
以四時爲柄，故事可勸也；以日星爲紀，故事可列也；月以爲量，故功有藝也。
是故先王慎所以感之者。故禮以道其志，樂以和其聲，政以一其行，刑以防其姦。禮樂刑政，其極一也，所以同民心而出治道也。
儒有今人與居，古人與稽；今世行之，後世以爲楷。
第貳場
論
translation_en:
…Han Hu, and representatives of Xu and Cao, at Guo. 〔First year of Duke Zhao〕
In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu. 〔Third year of Duke Xi〕
In autumn, Xun Wu of Jin led an army to attack Xianyu. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhao〕
The men of Qi returned to us the lands west of the Ji River. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xuan〕 The men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding〕
Record of Rites
Unify the Way and virtue in order to make customs uniform.
Use the four seasons as a handle, so that undertakings may be encouraged; use the sun and stars as a framework, so that undertakings may be ordered; use the moon as a measure, so that accomplishments may have defined limits.
For this reason, the former kings were careful about the means by which they moved the people. Thus ritual guides their intentions; music harmonizes their voices; government unifies their conduct; and punishments guard against their wrongdoing. Ritual, music, punishments, and government have a single ultimate aim: to unite the hearts of the people and bring forth the way of good governance.
There is a kind of Confucian scholar who lives among the people of the present but takes the ancients as his standard. His conduct in the present age becomes a model for later generations.
Second Session
Discourse

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
誠者聖人之本
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢令郡國求遺賢詔高帝十一年
擬唐以陸贄爲翰林學士誥建中四年
擬宋作邇英延義二閣成羣臣賀表景祐
二年
判語五條
講讀律令
收支留難
鄉飲酒禮
孳生馬匹
帶造段疋
===
第叁場
策五道
問自古帝王御世所以恢弘化理盜乂區
寓靡不以崇文教飭武備爲先蓋法天
之道以爲長久之術也然崇文不有本
而飭武不有要歟粤考往籍自陳君道
punctuated:
誠者，聖人之本。
詔誥表內科一道。
擬漢令郡國求遺賢詔，高帝十一年。
擬唐以陸贄爲翰林學士誥，建中四年。
擬宋作邇英延義二閣成羣臣賀表，景祐二年。
判語五條。
講讀律令。
收支留難。
鄉飲酒禮。
孳生馬匹。
帶造段疋。
第叁場
策五道。
問：自古帝王御世，所以恢弘化理、盜乂區寓，靡不以崇文教、飭武備爲先，蓋法天之道，以爲長久之術也。然崇文不有本，而飭武不有要歟？粤考往籍，自陳君道
translation_en:
“Sincerity is the foundation of the sage.”
One question from the categories of edict, mandate, and memorial [?].
Compose a hypothetical Han edict ordering the commanderies and kingdoms to seek out overlooked worthy men, dated the eleventh year of Emperor Gao’s reign.
Compose a hypothetical Tang mandate appointing Lu Zhi as a Hanlin Academician, dated the fourth year of Jianzhong.
Compose a hypothetical congratulatory memorial from the assembled officials of the Song upon completion of the Yingying and Yanyi pavilions, dated the second year of Jingyou.
Five legal judgments:
Lecturing on and reading the statutes and ordinances.
Obstructing receipts and disbursements.
The district drinking ceremony.
Breeding horses.
Manufacturing additional bolts of silk fabric [?].
Third Session
Five policy questions.
Question: From antiquity, emperors and kings governing the world have invariably given priority to promoting civil instruction and putting military preparations in order as the means to extend moral transformation and good government and bring peace to the realm [?]. In this they have modeled themselves on the Way of Heaven to devise a means of enduring rule. Yet does promoting civil culture not have a foundation, and does ordering military affairs not have an essential principle? Examining the records of the past, from the exposition of the ruler’s Way …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
克艱聖神文武典謨始賛夫云聖神文
武足矣必以廣運先之何歟然堯舜之
世比屋可封四夷來王所謂敷教徽典
誓師建長者其文武可想也抑尤有本
要所在歟夏后殷周之盛如曰揆奮曰
綏猷布昭曰顯謨承烈皆以文武言也
玆其所以比隆唐虞者歟漢唐若宋英
誼之辟非無文武可稱然或化有所雜
或威不大競何遂治不類古也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝開天肇紀遠契勳華當其櫜甲四
征卽首
建膠庠
親祀孔子及羣雄旣掃乃
制定府衞條練兵戎且凡所爲經文緯武者
聖訓
神謨周悉備至必有大本大要所在矣可得而
犟述之歟
貽燕鴻偉萬世率循若我
punctuated: 克艱，聖神文武，典謨始賛。夫云聖神文武足矣，必以廣運先之，何歟？然堯舜之世，比屋可封，四夷來王，所謂敷教徽典、誓師建長者，其文武可想也。抑尤有本要所在歟？夏后殷周之盛，如曰揆奮，曰綏猷布昭，曰顯謨承烈，皆以文武言也。玆其所以比隆唐虞者歟？漢唐若宋，英誼之辟，非無文武可稱，然或化有所雜，或威不大競，何遂治不類古也？洪惟我太祖高皇帝開天肇紀，遠契勳華，當其櫜甲四征，卽首建膠庠，親祀孔子；及羣雄旣掃，乃制定府衞，條練兵戎。且凡所爲經文緯武者，聖訓神謨，周悉備至，必有大本大要所在矣，可得而犟述之歟？貽燕鴻偉，萬世率循。若我
translation_en:
…to recognize the difficulty of ruling: sagacity, spiritual insight, and civil and martial virtue were first praised in the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents. Surely it would suffice to speak of sagacity, spiritual insight, and civil and martial virtue; why must these be preceded by “all-embracing and far-reaching”? In the age of Yao and Shun, every household had people worthy of enfeoffment, and the barbarians of the four quarters came to acknowledge their sovereignty. From such expressions as “spreading instruction through the splendid ordinances” and “addressing the troops and establishing leaders,” one can imagine their civil and martial achievements. Yet did these have some still more fundamental basis and essential principle? Of the flourishing Xia, Yin, and Zhou dynasties, such expressions as “assessing and rousing” [?], “bringing peace through plans and spreading enlightenment,” and “illustrious counsels and the continuation of achievements” all speak of civil and martial accomplishments. Was this how they equaled the splendor of Tang and Yu? Among the Han, Tang, and Song, there were outstanding and righteous rulers [?] whose civil and martial accomplishments deserved praise. Yet their transforming influence was sometimes adulterated, or their might failed to flourish greatly. Why, then, did their governance fall short of antiquity?

We reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao inaugurated a new order and founded the dynasty, matching the distant examples of Yao and Shun. While still bearing arms on campaigns in every direction, he gave priority to establishing schools and personally offered sacrifices to Confucius. Once the rival warlords had been swept away, he established the military commissions and guards and systematically trained the troops. Moreover, in everything he did to order civil affairs and organize military power, his sagely instructions and inspired counsels were comprehensive and complete. Surely these rested upon a great fundamental basis and a great essential principle. Can you expound these [?]? The legacy of peace he bequeathed was magnificent, to be followed through myriad generations. As for our …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
成祖文皇帝敦崇道化宣振英猷
世宗肅皇帝
文德誕敷
武功駿競尨背焯爍可頌述者何者與
聖祖同符歟欽惟
皇上臨御之始首
幸太學繼
躬大閱文武之業一時竝興眞憲
天法
===
祖媲美古昔保致太平之要圖也仰聞
聖學茂新
神東獨運自
臨雍閱武之外又有與
二祖
世宗默契者能窺測而名言歟諸士菁莪樂育
頌戴清寧久矣亦有可賛
獻於萬一者歟願恭陳之以鳴我
昭代之盛
punctuated: 成祖文皇帝敦崇道化，宣振英猷；世宗肅皇帝文德誕敷，武功駿競，尨背焯爍，可頌述者何者與聖祖同符歟？欽惟皇上臨御之始，首幸太學，繼躬大閱，文武之業一時竝興，眞憲天法祖、媲美古昔、保致太平之要圖也。仰聞聖學茂新，神東獨運，自臨雍閱武之外，又有與二祖、世宗默契者，能窺測而名言歟？諸士菁莪樂育，頌戴清寧久矣，亦有可賛獻於萬一者歟？願恭陳之，以鳴我昭代之盛。
translation_en:
… Emperor Wen, Chengzu, earnestly exalted moral transformation through the Way and proclaimed his illustrious designs; Emperor Su, Shizong, spread civil virtue far and wide and vigorously advanced military achievements. Among their resplendent accomplishments—the wording 尨背 is unclear [?]—which deeds worthy of praise and recounting matched those of the sagely founding emperor?

We reverently consider how, at the beginning of his reign, His Majesty first visited the Imperial University and subsequently conducted a grand military review in person. Civil and military undertakings flourished together: truly this was an essential plan for taking Heaven as his standard and his ancestors as his models, matching the excellence of antiquity, and securing great peace. We have respectfully heard that his sagely learning flourishes anew and his divine discernment operates independently [reading uncertain: 神東]. Beyond his visit to the Imperial University and review of the troops, are there further ways in which he tacitly accords with the two founding ancestors and Shizong? Can you discern and articulate them?

You scholars, joyfully nurtured like the luxuriant mugwort celebrated in the Odes, have long praised and gratefully enjoyed this peace and tranquillity. Might you offer even the smallest contribution to assist him? We ask you respectfully to set it forth, thereby giving voice to the flourishing glory of our illustrious age.

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
問道一而巳矣聖賢立言以明道顧不能
無異焉是不可不辨也子思作中庸首
發性命之說訓者謂天所賦爲命人所
受爲性矣何又曰所賦者氣所受者理
豈各有指歟孔子繫易始著道器之論
訓者謂形而上者爲理形而下者爲物
矣何又曰道亦器器亦道抑各有說歟
四端統於仁固也而有配以陰陽五行
四時者豈四端各自爲用歟性情統於
===
心固也而又指性之有形爲心性之有
動爲情者則心與情皆發自一性歟動
爲陽而靜爲陰孔子言知者動仁者靜
是陰陽各有屬矣而易傳乃謂知爲陰
而仁爲陽則動靜又何分歟巳爲體而
人爲用子思言成巳仁成物知是體用
各有在矣而朱子乃謂智自明而仁及
物則人巳果何別歟忠以盡巳信以盡
物理本相須者也而有以天道人道分
punctuated: 問：道一而巳矣，聖賢立言以明道，顧不能無異焉，是不可不辨也。子思作《中庸》，首發性命之說，訓者謂天所賦爲命，人所受爲性矣，何又曰所賦者氣，所受者理？豈各有指歟？孔子繫《易》，始著道器之論，訓者謂形而上者爲理，形而下者爲物矣，何又曰道亦器，器亦道？抑各有說歟？四端統於仁，固也，而有配以陰陽五行四時者，豈四端各自爲用歟？性情統於心，固也，而又指性之有形爲心，性之有動爲情者，則心與情皆發自一性歟？動爲陽而靜爲陰，孔子言知者動，仁者靜，是陰陽各有屬矣，而《易傳》乃謂知爲陰而仁爲陽，則動靜又何分歟？巳爲體而人爲用，子思言成巳仁，成物知，是體用各有在矣，而朱子乃謂智自明而仁及物，則人巳果何別歟？忠以盡巳，信以盡物，理本相須者也，而有以天道人道分
translation_en: Question: The Way is one, and that is all. The sages and worthies formulated their teachings to illuminate the Way, yet their statements could not be without differences. These must therefore be examined. When Zisi composed the Doctrine of the Mean, he began by setting forth the teaching concerning human nature and Heaven’s mandate. Commentators say that what Heaven endows is called the mandate, and what a person receives is called human nature. Why, then, do they also say that what is endowed is material force (qi), while what is received is principle (li)? Does each statement refer to something different? When Confucius appended his explanations to the Book of Changes, he first set forth the distinction between the Way and concrete things. Commentators say that what is above form is principle, and what is below form is a concrete thing. Why, then, do they also say that the Way is also concrete things, and concrete things are also the Way? Does each assertion have its own explanation? It is certainly true that the four moral beginnings are united in benevolence; yet some correlate them with yin and yang, the Five Phases, and the four seasons. Does each of the four beginnings, then, have its own distinct function? It is certainly true that human nature and the feelings are united in the mind; yet some identify human nature taking form as the mind, and human nature entering into activity as the feelings. Do the mind and the feelings, then, both issue from a single human nature? Activity is yang and stillness is yin. Confucius said that the wise are active and the benevolent are still. Thus yin and yang each have their respective associations. Yet the Commentary on the Changes says that wisdom is yin and benevolence is yang. How, then, are activity and stillness to be distinguished? The self is substance, and others are function. Zisi said that perfecting oneself is benevolence, and perfecting things is wisdom. Thus substance and function each have their respective sphere. Yet Master Zhu says that wisdom illuminates oneself and benevolence extends to things. What, then, is the actual distinction between others and oneself? Through wholeheartedness one fully realizes oneself, and through trustworthiness one fully realizes things: in principle, these depend upon one another. Yet there are those who distinguish them in terms of the Way of Heaven and the Way of humanity…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
言者何其辨之異耶知以明理行以履
事序不可紊者也而有謂知行互相發
者何其統之同耶夫學厭多岐道貴心
得凡此立言同異之間要皆身心切近
之學必有根極統會之所在也諸士涵
泳日久寧無反說窮理而自得於言語
之外者乎幸詳陳之
問仕學一理也學以基仕仕以行學養之
身心而發之事業寧有異致哉孔子之
===
言曰古之學者爲已今之學者爲人宋
儒以爲爲已者終至於成物爲人者終
至於喪已是又明學仕之相因而爲已
爲人之取效異矣粤自唐虞以迄周季
凡爲學者未有顯稱焉然夫子固必有
所指也其所謂學果何學而其所以爲
已爲人之辨也可無舉其大者而言之
歟自今觀之學既爲已則何所往而不
爲已也學既爲人則何所往而不爲人
punctuated:
言者，何其辨之異耶？知以明理，行以履事，序不可紊者也，而有謂知行互相發者，何其統之同耶？夫學厭多岐，道貴心得。凡此立言同異之間，要皆身心切近之學，必有根極統會之所在也。諸士涵泳日久，寧無反說窮理而自得於言語之外者乎？幸詳陳之。

問：仕學一理也，學以基仕，仕以行學，養之身心而發之事業，寧有異致哉？孔子之言曰：「古之學者爲已，今之學者爲人。」宋儒以爲，爲已者終至於成物，爲人者終至於喪已，是又明學仕之相因，而爲已、爲人之取效異矣。粤自唐虞以迄周季，凡爲學者未有顯稱焉，然夫子固必有所指也。其所謂學，果何學？而其所以爲已、爲人之辨也，可無舉其大者而言之歟？自今觀之，學既爲已，則何所往而不爲已也？學既爲人，則何所往而不爲人
translation_en:
…speak of them separately in these terms: why do they distinguish them so differently? Knowledge serves to illuminate principle, and action to carry out affairs; their sequence must not be confused. Yet some say that knowledge and action stimulate each other: why do they unite them in this way? Learning shuns divergent paths, while pursuit of the Way prizes personal understanding in the heart. Amid all these similarities and differences in formulation, the essential concern is learning that bears directly upon one's person and mind. There must be an ultimate root in which these teachings converge. You gentlemen have long immersed yourselves in study. Surely some of you, reflecting on these statements and investigating principle, have attained an understanding beyond words? Please set it out in detail.

Question: Holding office and learning follow a single principle. Learning lays the foundation for officeholding, and officeholding puts learning into practice. What is cultivated in one's person and mind finds expression in one's undertakings: how could their purposes differ? Confucius said: “Learners of antiquity studied for themselves; learners today study for others.” The Confucian scholars of the Song held that those who study for themselves ultimately bring other things to fulfillment, whereas those who study for others ultimately lose themselves. This further clarifies the mutual dependence of learning and officeholding, while showing that studying for oneself and studying for others yield different results. From the ages of Tang and Yu down to the closing years of the Zhou, no learners were expressly identified in these terms [?]. Yet the Master must surely have had particular people in mind. What precisely was the learning of which he spoke? And concerning his distinction between studying for oneself and studying for others, can you refrain from presenting and discussing its chief points? Viewed from the present, if one's learning is for oneself, wherever one goes, will it not remain for oneself? If one's learning is for others, wherever one goes, will it not remain for others…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
也夫子之言盡矣漢隋而下儒者又有
謂古之仕者養人今之仕者養巳古之
仕者爲人今之仕者爲巳雖不過彷彿
夫子人巳之言而辨析古今用世之殊
也然於夫子論學之旨亦有所當歟否
歟而古今仕之爲人養人也爲巳養巳
也或由其學之所爲不同而然歟抑别
有說歟自三代以迄漢隋而下其仕之
爲古也今也人固不可殫述矣然其養
===
人養巳爲人爲巳之仕豈無可略舉其
著者以爲取舍之極歟諸士辨志正學
行且有仕道之責願以夙所得於古今
之判而體認乎聖賢之訓者明以告我
問士君子之處世其出處去就皆有大閑
不可以或踰也古伊呂孔孟大聖大賢
尚矣姑自後世之昭在簡冊者試一訂
焉以出處言之商山采芝富春垂釣均
之抗節於不臣也其所守果皆固歟安
punctuated:
也。夫子之言盡矣。漢隋而下，儒者又有謂：「古之仕者養人，今之仕者養巳；古之仕者爲人，今之仕者爲巳。」雖不過彷彿夫子人巳之言，而辨析古今用世之殊也。然於夫子論學之旨，亦有所當歟？否歟？而古今仕之爲人養人也，爲巳養巳也，或由其學之所爲不同而然歟？抑别有說歟？自三代以迄漢隋而下，其仕之爲古也、今也，人固不可殫述矣。然其養人養巳、爲人爲巳之仕，豈無可略舉其著者，以爲取舍之極歟？諸士辨志正學，行且有仕道之責，願以夙所得於古今之判，而體認乎聖賢之訓者，明以告我。

問：士君子之處世，其出處去就皆有大閑，不可以或踰也。古伊呂孔孟，大聖大賢，尚矣。姑自後世之昭在簡冊者，試一訂焉。以出處言之，商山采芝，富春垂釣，均之抗節於不臣也，其所守果皆固歟？安
translation_en:
…The Master's words exhaust the matter. From the Han and Sui onward, Confucian scholars have also said: “Those who served in antiquity provided for others; those who serve today provide for themselves. Those who served in antiquity acted for others; those who serve today act for themselves.” Although this merely echoes the Master's words about others and oneself, it distinguishes how men of antiquity and of the present differ in taking an active role in the world. Yet does it accord in some measure with the Master's meaning in discussing learning, or does it not? As for serving others and providing for others, or serving oneself and providing for oneself, in official service ancient and modern: do these differences perhaps arise from different purposes in learning? Or is there another explanation? From the Three Dynasties through the Han and Sui and afterward, those whose service exemplifies the ancient or the modern approach certainly cannot all be recounted. Yet among officials who provided for others or themselves, and acted for others or themselves, could we not briefly cite some outstanding examples as the ultimate standard for what to embrace and what to reject? You candidates distinguish your aspirations and set your learning aright; soon you will bear the responsibilities of official service. I ask you to explain clearly to me what you have long understood concerning this distinction between antiquity and the present, and what you have grasped through reflection upon the teachings of the sages and worthies.

Question: As scholars and gentlemen conduct themselves in the world, there are fundamental bounds governing their entry into service or retirement, their withdrawal or acceptance of office, which must never be transgressed. The great sages and worthies of antiquity—Yi Yin, Lü Shang, Kongzi, and Mengzi—stand far above us. Let us provisionally examine some figures of later ages whose deeds are clearly recorded in the historical writings. Speaking of entering service or remaining in retirement: those who gathered fungi on Mount Shang and the man who fished at Fuchun alike upheld their integrity by refusing to become subjects. Were they indeed all steadfast in what they maintained? An…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
石不出深源不起均之繫望於一時也
其所成果皆副歟就徵爲諫議大夫應
聘爲中郎將其拜命同也何俱來友人
之責招以手敕而不出拜爲拾遺而不
起其自守同也何俱貽出位之譏衡山
歸隱矣胡復有觀察之行終南自樂矣
乃竟赴司諫之召凡此所以見於人已
之間者昔人固已論之矣可述而言之
歟以去就言之乞骸遺歸稱知足矣又
有受爵而朝朔望者意何在也絕迹梁
碭稱見幾矣又有不去而甘黨獄者見
何殊也感秋風而興歎志固有在也視
夫賦歸去來而飄然長往者得無同歟
解樞職而勇退心固有爲也視夫成都
乞歸而控疏辭召者得無異歟優游綠
野之堂矣何反取浮沉之譏從容獨樂
之園矣何復就僕射之命凡此所以爲
心迹之辨者昔人亦已評之矣可指而
punctuated: 石不出，深源不起，均之繫望於一時也，其所成果皆副歟？就徵爲諫議大夫，應聘爲中郎將，其拜命同也，何俱來友人之責？招以手敕而不出，拜爲拾遺而不起，其自守同也，何俱貽出位之譏？衡山歸隱矣，胡復有觀察之行？終南自樂矣，乃竟赴司諫之召！凡此所以見於人已之間者，昔人固已論之矣，可述而言之歟？以去就言之，乞骸遺歸，稱知足矣，又有受爵而朝朔望者，意何在也？絕迹梁碭，稱見幾矣，又有不去而甘黨獄者，見何殊也？感秋風而興歎，志固有在也，視夫賦歸去來而飄然長往者，得無同歟？解樞職而勇退，心固有爲也，視夫成都乞歸而控疏辭召者，得無異歟？優游綠野之堂矣，何反取浮沉之譏？從容獨樂之園矣，何復就僕射之命？凡此所以爲心迹之辨者，昔人亦已評之矣，可指而
translation_en:
…Anshi did not come forward to serve, and Shenyuan did not take office: both were men on whom the hopes of their age rested. Did their accomplishments in fact fulfill those hopes? One answered a summons to become Grand Master of Remonstrance; another accepted an invitation to become Leader of Court Gentlemen. They were alike in accepting appointment: why did both incur reproaches from their friends? One would not come forward despite an imperial summons written in the emperor’s own hand; another would not take office when appointed Reminder. They were alike in holding to their principles: why did both invite criticism for overstepping their station? One had retired into seclusion at Hengshan: why did he subsequently set out to serve as Surveillance Commissioner? Another was content at Zhongnan, yet ultimately answered a summons to become Director of Remonstrance! Earlier writers have already discussed all these matters concerning oneself and others [?]. Can you recount and explain their judgments?
As for leaving or remaining in office: one begged leave to retire and was sent home [?], winning praise for knowing when he had enough; yet there was also one who accepted a noble title and attended court on the first and fifteenth days of the month. What was his intention? One withdrew entirely into Liang and Dang, winning praise for discerning the first signs of danger; yet there was also one who refused to leave and willingly faced imprisonment in a factional prosecution. How did their perceptions differ? One sighed upon feeling the autumn wind: his aspirations certainly lay elsewhere. Compared with the man who composed “Returning Home” and departed freely for good, was he not similar? One relinquished his post in the Bureau of Military Affairs and resolutely retired: he certainly had reasons of his own. Compared with the man who sought leave to return home from Chengdu and submitted memorials declining a summons, was he not different? One passed his days at ease in the Hall of Green Fields: why did he instead earn criticism for drifting with the times? Another lived serenely in the Garden of Solitary Enjoyment: why did he again accept appointment as Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs? Earlier writers have also assessed all these matters in distinguishing inward intentions from outward conduct. Can you identify and…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
言之歟自今觀之其中亦有不詭於道
而無愧於古者歟抑自數子之外尚有
出處去就合道而可言者否也夫論入
於三代之下固難律以聖賢之全然品
騭乎百世之前要亦必有大中之矩矣
試詳言之以觀尚論之學
問漢儒有言善聲而不知轉未可謂能歌
也善言而不知變未可謂能說也蓋言
未有不通變而能宜民者矣貴入我
===
國朝始創藩省諸所建置一視中土蓋二百
年於茲矣試以今日通變之所宜先者
商之兵所以制夷也勾取日艱而逃亡
愈衆何以為足伍之圖糧所以餉兵也
額濟歲虧而糜費愈增何以為盈賦之
術館馬之輸銀有限而代役者苦於賠
貱之不勝何策以蘇之站伍之尺籍無
幾而見存者困於送迎之日倍何道以
逸之有田皆山也浹旬不雨歲且不入
punctuated:
言之歟？自今觀之，其中亦有不詭於道而無愧於古者歟？抑自數子之外，尚有出處去就合道而可言者否也？夫論入於三代之下，固難律以聖賢之全，然品騭乎百世之前，要亦必有大中之矩矣。試詳言之，以觀尚論之學。
問：漢儒有言：「善聲而不知轉，未可謂能歌也；善言而不知變，未可謂能說也。」蓋言未有不通變而能宜民者矣。貴入我國朝，始創藩省，諸所建置，一視中土，蓋二百年於茲矣。試以今日通變之所宜先者商之。兵所以制夷也，勾取日艱，而逃亡愈衆，何以為足伍之圖？糧所以餉兵也，額濟歲虧，而糜費愈增，何以為盈賦之術？館馬之輸銀有限，而代役者苦於賠貱之不勝，何策以蘇之？站伍之尺籍無幾，而見存者困於送迎之日倍，何道以逸之？有田皆山也，浹旬不雨，歲且不入，
translation_en:
…can you identify them and discuss them? Viewed from the present, were there among them any whose conduct did not depart from the Way and who need feel no shame before the ancients? Or, beyond these several men, were there others whose entering or withdrawing from office, departing or remaining, accorded with the Way and deserve discussion? When discussing times after the Three Dynasties, it is certainly difficult to judge men by the full perfection of sages and worthies. Yet in appraising those who lived a hundred generations ago, there must nevertheless be a standard of perfect impartiality. Explain this in detail, so that we may assess your learning in judging the men of antiquity.
Question: A Han Confucian scholar said: “One who has a fine voice but does not know how to modulate it cannot yet be called a skilled singer; one who speaks well but does not know how to adapt cannot yet be called a skilled persuader.” This means that no one can benefit the people without adapting to changing circumstances. Only after Guizhou came under our dynasty was a provincial administration first established there. All its institutions were established on the same footing as those of the central lands, and it has now been some two hundred years. Consider which adaptations should take priority today. Troops are the means of controlling the non-Han peoples. Yet requisitioning men to fill military service obligations grows harder by the day, while deserters grow ever more numerous. How can the ranks be brought up to strength? Grain is the means of provisioning the troops. Yet the stipulated supplies fall short year after year, while wasteful expenditure continually increases. By what means can the revenue quota be met? Silver payments for the horses at the relay lodgings are limited, while those performing the service in others’ stead suffer from unbearable obligations to cover the shortfalls [?]. What policy could relieve them? Few men are entered on the relay-station service registers, and those actually present are burdened by the daily multiplication of escort and reception duties. How can they be given respite? All the fields lie in the mountains; if no rain falls for ten full days, there may be no harvest for the year …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
非疏築之未豫乎有民皆夷也釁校竝
興擴戾自若非化導之未至乎權不一
則事不集議者欲以川湖之兼轄而專
隷焉其舉果無滯歟化不更則患不彌
議者欲於土司之梗化而改流焉其圖
果可永歟夫善救弊者善守法者也諸
生抱經濟之術必切梓里之憂則所謂
善聲而轉善言而變者宜莫先於此矣
其條著於篇當事者將有採焉
punctuated: 非疏築之未豫乎？有民皆夷也，釁校竝興，擴戾自若，非化導之未至乎？權不一則事不集，議者欲以川湖之兼轄而專隷焉，其舉果無滯歟？化不更則患不彌，議者欲於土司之梗化而改流焉，其圖果可永歟？夫善救弊者，善守法者也。諸生抱經濟之術，必切梓里之憂，則所謂善聲而轉、善言而變者，宜莫先於此矣。其條著於篇，當事者將有採焉。
translation_en:
…is this not because dredging and construction of embankments have not been undertaken in advance? The inhabitants are all indigenous peoples; disputes and conflicts arise together, and their unruliness persists [?]. Is this not because efforts to instruct and transform them have fallen short? Unless authority is unified, affairs cannot be accomplished. Some propose replacing the overlapping jurisdiction of Sichuan and Huguang with exclusive jurisdiction under a single authority. Would this measure truly encounter no obstacles? Unless the system of governance is changed, troubles will not subside. Some propose replacing native officials who resist civilizing instruction with regular officials appointed by the central government. Would this plan truly provide a lasting solution?

Those skilled at remedying abuses are skilled at upholding the laws. You students possess the arts of ordering the realm and aiding its people, and must feel keen concern for your native places. Thus, in what is called turning toward good counsel and changing in response to good words, surely nothing should take precedence over these matters. Set out your proposals point by point in your essays; those responsible for these affairs may adopt some of them.
