title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子易事而難說也說之不以道不說也
及其使人也器之
陳時言
同考試官教諭謝　批　發明君子易事難說處親
切
考試官教諭陳　批　詞意明盡可式
考試官教授吳　批　莊重精瑩
===
聖人辨君子事說之難易所以昭公恕之心也
蓋君子以公恕存心者也則其於事說之間而
豈無難易之辨乎夫子之意若曰君子之不可
及者存心而已矣君子之存心者公與恕而已
矣彼君子居夫民物之上其位可以奔走乎人
也則必有為君子之役而事之者矣人知所以
事君子而不知其事之易焉其勢可以號令乎
人也則必有投君子之喜而說之者矣人知所
以說君子而不知其說之難焉是故有說之不
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「君子易事而難說也，說之不以道，不說也；及其使人也，器之。」
陳時言
同考試官教諭謝批：發明君子易事難說處，親切。
考試官教諭陳批：詞意明盡，可式。
考試官教授吳批：莊重精瑩。

聖人辨君子事說之難易，所以昭公恕之心也。蓋君子以公恕存心者也，則其於事說之間，而豈無難易之辨乎？夫子之意若曰：君子之不可及者，存心而已矣；君子之存心者，公與恕而已矣。彼君子居夫民物之上，其位可以奔走乎人也，則必有為君子之役而事之者矣。人知所以事君子，而不知其事之易焉。其勢可以號令乎人也，則必有投君子之喜而說之者矣。人知所以說君子，而不知其說之難焉。是故有說之不
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“A gentleman is easy to serve but difficult to please. If one seeks to please him contrary to the Way, he is not pleased; when he employs others, he assigns them duties according to their capacities.”
Chen Shiyan
Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of how the gentleman is easy to serve but difficult to please is apt and direct.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The language and meaning are clear and fully developed; this may serve as a model.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “Dignified, refined, and lucid.”

The Sage distinguished the ease and difficulty of serving and pleasing a gentleman in order to illuminate his impartial and considerate heart. For the gentleman cherishes impartiality and consideration in his heart: could there then be no distinction between ease and difficulty when it comes to serving and pleasing him? The Master's meaning might be expressed thus: what makes the gentleman beyond others’ reach is simply the disposition of his heart; what the gentleman cherishes in his heart is simply impartiality and consideration.

The gentleman occupies a position above the people and all things. His rank enables him to command others’ service, so there will necessarily be those who labor for the gentleman and serve him. People know how to serve the gentleman, but do not understand how easy he is to serve. His authority enables him to issue commands to others, so there will necessarily be those who appeal to the gentleman’s likes and seek to please him. People know how to please the gentleman, but do not understand how difficult he is to please. Thus, there are those who seek to please him in a way that is not…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
以道者其情則順其理則逆所謂說之難者正
以其於是而有不狥焉耳吾見中之以心之所
甚欲而以其至剛者裁之則巽者適以爲拂也
逆之以意之所甚喜而以其至正者臨之則順
者適以爲忤也蓋以理御情而不以情廢天下
之理矣其難說也何如有才之不能全者宜於
彼或不宜於此所謂事之易者正以其於是而
不求備焉耳吾見可以小知者則小用之而俾
經理乎庶務之繁也可以大受者則大用之而
===
俾負荷乎國家之重也蓋以才任事而不以事
責天下之才矣其易事也何如是則不說所易
說者自人以爲難說而非君子有心於難之也
不責備於人者自人以爲易事而非君子有心
於易之也此其公恕之心可見而豈小人之私
且刻者所能及乎抑論君子之心主於道而已
矣故事之易者其說未嘗不難說之難者其事
未嘗不易蓋相因而不相悖也夫子使求爲宰
使由治其賦而衞卿之位彌子不能說而主之
punctuated: 以道者，其情則順，其理則逆。所謂說之難者，正以其於是而有不狥焉耳。吾見中之以心之所甚欲，而以其至剛者裁之，則巽者適以爲拂也；逆之以意之所甚喜，而以其至正者臨之，則順者適以爲忤也。蓋以理御情，而不以情廢天下之理矣。其難說也何如？有才之不能全者，宜於彼，或不宜於此。所謂事之易者，正以其於是而不求備焉耳。吾見可以小知者，則小用之，而俾經理乎庶務之繁也；可以大受者，則大用之，而俾負荷乎國家之重也。蓋以才任事，而不以事責天下之才矣。其易事也何如？是則不說所易說者，自人以爲難說，而非君子有心於難之也；不責備於人者，自人以爲易事，而非君子有心於易之也。此其公恕之心可見，而豈小人之私且刻者所能及乎？抑論君子之心，主於道而已矣。故事之易者，其說未嘗不難；說之難者，其事未嘗不易。蓋相因而不相悖也。夫子使求爲宰，使由治其賦，而衞卿之位，彌子不能說而主之
translation_en:
…[attempts to please him that do not accord] with the Way may gratify his feelings, but run counter to principle. What is meant by his being difficult to please is precisely that, in such cases, he refuses to yield. I see that when someone seeks to win him over with what his heart most desires, he judges it with utmost firmness, so that the apparent deference instead becomes an affront. When someone anticipates his wishes with what most delights him, he confronts it with utmost rectitude, so that the apparent compliance instead becomes an offense. Thus he governs his feelings by principle, rather than allowing his feelings to set aside the principles of the world. How difficult he is to please!

There are people whose abilities are not comprehensive: they may be suited to one task but unsuited to another. What is meant by his being easy to serve is precisely that, in such cases, he does not demand perfection. I see that those whose abilities can be appreciated in small matters he employs in minor duties, having them manage the complexities of everyday affairs; those who can be entrusted with great responsibilities he employs in major duties, having them shoulder the weighty affairs of the state. Thus he assigns duties according to ability, rather than demanding that the talents of the world meet every requirement of a task. How easy he is to serve!

Accordingly, when he takes no pleasure in what would readily please others, people themselves consider him difficult to please; the gentleman does not deliberately make himself difficult. When he does not demand perfection of others, people themselves consider him easy to serve; the gentleman does not deliberately make himself easy. Here his impartiality and consideration for others become apparent. How could the selfishness and harshness of the petty man ever match them?

To consider the gentleman’s heart further, it is devoted solely to the Way. Thus, though he is easy to serve, he is always difficult to please; though he is difficult to please, he is always easy to serve. These qualities sustain rather than contradict one another. The Master had Qiu serve as steward and had You administer military levies; yet, as for a ministerial post in Wei, Mizi could not win his favor and act as his patron …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
則事說之難易可以想見矣故曰孔子聖之時
好學近乎知力行近乎仁知恥近乎勇知
斯三者則知所以脩身
張志皐
同考試官教諭馬　批　入德脩身之旨發揮殆盡
錄之
考試官教諭陳　批　清順之作
考試官教授吳　批　明暢
===
中庸指入德之方而因明身之所由脩也夫脩
身必本於德也既知入德之方則所以脩其身
者豈外是而得之哉中庸之意謂夫人君以脩
身爲本脩身以進德爲先知仁勇固爲天下之
達德矣而求所以進之者則何如哉彼知以明
道吾知之未能也而務學以窮其理恒亹亹而
不厭焉則聞見既博智慮由之以漸啓矣於知
不亦近乎仁以體道吾仁之未能也而躬行以
履其事毎乾乾而不已焉則體驗日熟私意由
之以漸忘矣於仁不亦近乎勇以强乎道吾未
punctuated:
則事說之難易可以想見矣。故曰：「孔子，聖之時。」

好學近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇。知斯三者，則知所以脩身。

張志皐

同考試官教諭馬批：「入德脩身之旨，發揮殆盡，錄之。」
考試官教諭陳批：「清順之作。」
考試官教授吳批：「明暢。」

中庸指入德之方，而因明身之所由脩也。夫脩身必本於德也，既知入德之方，則所以脩其身者，豈外是而得之哉？中庸之意謂夫人君以脩身爲本，脩身以進德爲先。知仁勇固爲天下之達德矣，而求所以進之者，則何如哉？彼知以明道，吾知之未能也，而務學以窮其理，恒亹亹而不厭焉，則聞見既博，智慮由之以漸啓矣，於知不亦近乎？仁以體道，吾仁之未能也，而躬行以履其事，毎乾乾而不已焉，則體驗日熟，私意由之以漸忘矣，於仁不亦近乎？勇以强乎道，吾未
translation_en:
…then one can readily imagine how difficult or easy it is to serve and to please him. Thus it is said: “Confucius was the sage who acted according to the times.”

“To love learning is to approach wisdom; to exert oneself in practice is to approach humaneness; to know shame is to approach courage. Knowing these three, one knows how to cultivate oneself.”

Zhang Zhigao 張志皐

Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of entering into virtue and cultivating oneself is expounded almost exhaustively. Select this essay.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “A clear and fluent composition.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “Lucid and flowing.”

The Doctrine of the Mean indicates the means of entering into virtue and thereby clarifies how the self is cultivated. Self-cultivation must be rooted in virtue. Once one knows the means of entering into virtue, how could the means of cultivating oneself be found outside these? The intent of the Doctrine of the Mean is that the ruler takes self-cultivation as his foundation, and that self-cultivation gives priority to advancing in virtue. Wisdom, humaneness, and courage are indeed the universally applicable virtues of the world. But how does one seek the means of advancing in them?

Wisdom serves to illuminate the Way. If I have not yet attained wisdom, but devote myself to learning in order to investigate its principles fully, constantly applying myself without weariness, then, as my learning and experience broaden, my understanding and reflection will gradually develop through them. Is this not to approach wisdom?

Humaneness serves to embody the Way. If I have not yet attained humaneness, but personally put its requirements into practice, always striving diligently without cease, then, as my understanding through experience grows more practiced each day, selfish intentions will gradually be forgotten. Is this not to approach humaneness?

Courage serves to hold firmly to the Way. I have not yet…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
能勇也而知行之不若人恒用以爲恥焉則羞
惡中存剛毅由之以日奮矣於勇不亦近乎夫
是三者固求進於達德之事而爲體道成身之
原也人患未之知耳苟能於此三者知至至之
而向往之不迷知終終之而交脩之不怠則功
之深者德之所由以進也而慎脩之要以存德
之立者道之所由以行也而正己之功斯盡天
下同得之理以一身而統會之所以建其有極
而示萬邦之儀刑者此也天下共由之理以一
===
身而兼體之所以端其道揆而樹萬民之表則
者此也孰謂脩身之道不於三近而得之哉取
人以立政者宜知所勉矣抑論三近所以脩身
而夫子又云齊明盛服非禮不動何歟此則所
謂敬也自身之已脩者而言也吁曰敬止曰敬
勝者文武之心法也心法得而治法可舉也使
哀公知所勉焉則魯其東周而萬世君天下之
法程在是矣
子路人告之以有過則喜禹聞善言則拜
punctuated:
能勇也，而知行之不若人，恒用以爲恥焉，則羞惡中存，剛毅由之以日奮矣，於勇不亦近乎？夫是三者，固求進於達德之事，而爲體道成身之原也。人患未之知耳。苟能於此三者，知至至之，而向往之不迷；知終終之，而交脩之不怠，則功之深者，德之所由以進也，而慎脩之要以存；德之立者，道之所由以行也，而正己之功斯盡。天下同得之理，以一身而統會之，所以建其有極而示萬邦之儀刑者，此也；天下共由之理，以一身而兼體之，所以端其道揆而樹萬民之表則者，此也。孰謂脩身之道不於三近而得之哉？取人以立政者，宜知所勉矣。抑論三近所以脩身，而夫子又云「齊明盛服，非禮不動」，何歟？此則所謂敬也，自身之已脩者而言也。吁！曰「敬止」，曰「敬勝」者，文武之心法也。心法得而治法可舉也。使哀公知所勉焉，則魯其東周，而萬世君天下之法程在是矣。

子路人告之以有過則喜，禹聞善言則拜，
translation_en:
…have not yet attained courage, but if I recognize that my knowledge and conduct fall short of others’ and constantly regard this as shameful, then a sense of shame and aversion to wrongdoing will abide within me, and firmness and resolve will grow more vigorous each day. Is this not to draw near to courage? These three practices are indeed ways of seeking progress toward the universally applicable virtues, and they are the source of embodying the Way and perfecting oneself. The trouble is simply that people do not understand them. If, in these three matters, one knows what one must reach and reaches it, pursuing it without losing direction, and knows what one must complete and completes it, cultivating all three together without flagging, then deepening effort provides the means for advancing virtue, and the essentials of diligent self-cultivation are preserved. Established virtue provides the means for putting the Way into practice, and the work of rectifying oneself is thereby fulfilled. To gather into one’s own person the principles that all under Heaven alike possess—this is how one establishes the supreme standard and displays a model for the myriad states. To embody fully in one’s own person the principles that all under Heaven follow—this is how one sets right the moral standards of governance and establishes an exemplar for the myriad people. Who could say that the way of self-cultivation is not attained through these three approaches to virtue? Those who select men to establish good government should know where to direct their efforts.

Yet, when discussing how these three approaches serve self-cultivation, why does the Master also say, “Purify yourself, be clear-minded, wear full ceremonial dress, and make no movement contrary to ritual propriety”? This is what is called reverence, spoken of from the standpoint of one whose person is already cultivated. Ah! “Abide in reverence” and “Let reverence prevail”—these express the method of cultivating the mind transmitted by Kings Wen and Wu. Once this method of cultivating the mind is grasped, the methods of government can be put into practice. Had Duke Ai known where to direct his efforts, Lu might have become an Eastern Zhou; and herein lies the enduring model for those who rule all under Heaven.

When someone told Zilu that he had a fault, he rejoiced; when Yu heard good words, he bowed …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
大舜有大焉善與人同舍己從人樂取
於人以爲善
胡夢豸
同考試官學正陳　批　聖賢樂善之誠講中識輕
重且渾融無迹
考試官教諭陳　批　講大舜公善處意融而詞
暢
考試官教授吴　批　整潔
大賢敘聖賢之樂善而深賛虞帝之大焉蓋善
===
必公於天下而後爲大也此大賢所以歷敘由
禹而深有取於舜也歟昔孟子之意蓋謂好善
者夫人之同情公善者聖人之極致吾玆有感
於古之聖賢矣彼以子路之賢雖未立於無過
而其心則勇於有聞者故人告之以過則喜焉
蓋深幸遷善之有機而不難於反己以圖之者
矣子路之樂善何其誠耶以大禹之聖雖若無
資於人而其心則不自滿假者故一聞善言則
拜焉蓋深慶致理之有助而不覺其屈己以受
punctuated:
大舜有大焉，善與人同，舍己從人，樂取於人以爲善。
胡夢豸
同考試官學正陳，批：聖賢樂善之誠，講中識輕重，且渾融無迹。
考試官教諭陳，批：講大舜公善處，意融而詞暢。
考試官教授吴，批：整潔。
大賢敘聖賢之樂善，而深賛虞帝之大焉。蓋善必公於天下而後爲大也，此大賢所以歷敘由、禹而深有取於舜也歟！昔孟子之意，蓋謂好善者，夫人之同情；公善者，聖人之極致。吾玆有感於古之聖賢矣。彼以子路之賢，雖未立於無過，而其心則勇於有聞者，故人告之以過則喜焉。蓋深幸遷善之有機，而不難於反己以圖之者矣。子路之樂善何其誠耶！以大禹之聖，雖若無資於人，而其心則不自滿假者，故一聞善言則拜焉。蓋深慶致理之有助，而不覺其屈己以受
translation_en:
…The great Shun was greater still: he shared goodness with others, set aside his own views to follow others, and delighted in drawing upon others to practice goodness.

Hu Mengzhi 胡夢豸

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor: “The exposition of the sincerity with which sages and worthies delight in goodness shows discernment in assigning due weight to each point; it is also seamlessly integrated, without visible traces of artifice.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: “In explaining how the great Shun shared goodness with all, the ideas are well integrated and the language flows freely.”

Comment by Examiner Wu, School Instructor: “Orderly and polished.”

The great worthy recounts the delight that sages and worthies take in goodness, and deeply praises the greatness of the sovereign of Yu. For goodness becomes great only when it is shared with all under Heaven. Is this not why the great worthy recounts in turn the examples of You and Yu, yet finds still more to commend in Shun?

Mencius’s meaning was, it seems, that loving goodness is a feeling common to everyone, whereas sharing goodness with all is the highest attainment of the sage. Here I am moved by the sages and worthies of antiquity. Worthy though Zilu was, he had not yet reached a state of being without faults; yet his heart was eager to hear of them. Thus, when someone told him of a fault, he rejoiced. He felt deeply fortunate to have an opportunity to advance toward goodness, and did not find it difficult to turn inward and strive for it. How sincere was Zilu’s delight in goodness!

Sagely though the great Yu was, and seemingly without need to draw upon others, his heart was neither complacent nor self-important. Thus, whenever he heard good words, he bowed. He deeply rejoiced at receiving help in bringing about good government, and, without being conscious of humbling himself, accepted…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
之者矣禹之樂善何其誠耶然善非已之善也
聞過而喜則尤未至於忘已善非人之善也聞
言而拜則尤未至於忘人未大也若大舜不猶
有大於是乎亦惟擴吾大同之量以會其大公
之理而已是故德至於舜已固無不善矣而自
其謙以受益之心視之則惟知不足之在已而
舍已以從乎人初無一毫繫吝之私也其以已
之善而同諸人者乎人之善亦未必能如舜矣
而自其沛然順應之心視之則惟知有餘之在
===
人而取之以用於已初無一毫勉强之迹也其
以人之善而同諸已者乎此則合人已於兩忘
視夫喜聞過而猶知有已者何如也融物我於
無迹視夫拜善言而猶知有人者何如也斯舜
之所以為大也歟抑此天道也天惟有於穆不
已之誠而含弘光大也故能納萬有以成覆物
之功聖人惟其誠而明通公溥也故能涵萬善
以普及物之化然則均一樂善之誠也子路誠
之者也禹則明而誠者也舜則誠者也故曰聞
punctuated: 之者矣。禹之樂善何其誠耶！然善非已之善也，聞過而喜，則尤未至於忘已；善非人之善也，聞言而拜，則尤未至於忘人。未大也。若大舜，不猶有大於是乎？亦惟擴吾大同之量，以會其大公之理而已。是故德至於舜，已固無不善矣，而自其謙以受益之心視之，則惟知不足之在已，而舍已以從乎人，初無一毫繫吝之私也。其以已之善而同諸人者乎？人之善亦未必能如舜矣，而自其沛然順應之心視之，則惟知有餘之在人，而取之以用於已，初無一毫勉强之迹也。其以人之善而同諸已者乎？此則合人已於兩忘，視夫喜聞過而猶知有已者何如也？融物我於無迹，視夫拜善言而猶知有人者何如也？斯舜之所以為大也歟！抑此天道也。天惟有於穆不已之誠，而含弘光大也，故能納萬有以成覆物之功。聖人惟其誠，而明通公溥也，故能涵萬善以普及物之化。然則均一樂善之誠也，子路誠之者也，禹則明而誠者也，舜則誠者也。故曰：「聞
translation_en: …receive it. How sincere was Yu’s delight in goodness! Yet goodness is not the exclusive possession of oneself: to rejoice upon hearing of one’s faults is still not to have reached self-forgetfulness. Nor is goodness the exclusive possession of others: to bow upon hearing good words is still not to have forgotten others. This is not yet greatness. Was there not something still greater in the great Shun? It was simply to enlarge one’s capacity for embracing all in unity, thereby apprehending the principle of perfect impartiality. Thus, when virtue reached the level of Shun, there was certainly nothing in himself that was not good. Yet, viewed from his humble readiness to benefit from others, he knew only his own inadequacy and set himself aside to follow others, without the slightest selfish attachment or reluctance. Was this not to make his own goodness one with that of others? Others’ goodness might not necessarily equal Shun’s. Yet, viewed from his abundant and responsive disposition, he knew only what others possessed in surplus and drew upon it for his own use, without the slightest trace of forced effort. Was this not to make others’ goodness one with his own? This unites others and oneself in the forgetting of both: how does it compare with delighting in hearing of one’s faults while still remaining conscious of oneself? It merges things and self without a trace of distinction: how does it compare with bowing before good words while still remaining conscious of others? Is this not what made Shun great? Indeed, this is the Way of Heaven. Heaven possesses a profound and unceasing sincerity, encompassing, expansive, radiant, and great; thus it can embrace all that exists and accomplish its work of sheltering all things. The sage, through his sincerity, is discerning, all-penetrating, impartial, and all-embracing; thus he can contain every goodness and extend his transforming influence universally to all things. Their sincerity in delighting in goodness is therefore one and the same. Zilu was one who strove to become sincere; Yu attained sincerity through understanding; Shun was inherently sincere. Thus it is said: “To hear …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
過可賢又曰聖同天
易
君子體仁足以長人嘉會足以合禮利物
足以和義貞固足以幹事君子行此四
德者故曰乾元亨利貞
張志皐
考試官教諭陳　批　乾道至教君子至德此作
能發明之宜錄以式
考試官教授吳　批　詞切實而意明盡是深於
易者
===
觀君子盡性由於健而經文繫乾之義可識矣
蓋四德之全非至健不能也觀諸君子而經文
之義不可識哉文言之意若曰天命之性同具
於吾人盡性之功獨歸於君子君子之盡性何
如彼元之理在於人則爲仁君子以仁存心而
措諸身者莫非仁道之充周則惠愛所及而物
皆庋內矣不足以長人乎亨之理在於人則爲
禮君子以禮物身而接乎人者莫非典禮之會
punctuated:
過可賢，又曰聖同天。

易

君子體仁足以長人，嘉會足以合禮，利物足以和義，貞固足以幹事。君子行此四德者，故曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」

張志皐

考試官教諭陳批：乾道至教，君子至德，此作能發明之，宜錄以式。

考試官教授吳批：詞切實而意明盡，是深於易者。

觀君子盡性由於健，而經文繫乾之義可識矣。蓋四德之全，非至健不能也。觀諸君子，而經文之義不可識哉？文言之意若曰：天命之性，同具於吾人；盡性之功，獨歸於君子。君子之盡性何如？彼元之理，在於人則爲仁。君子以仁存心，而措諸身者，莫非仁道之充周，則惠愛所及，而物皆庋內矣，不足以長人乎？亨之理，在於人則爲禮。君子以禮物身，而接乎人者，莫非典禮之會
translation_en:
…faults, one can become worthy”; it also says, “The sage is one with Heaven.”

Book of Changes

“The gentleman embodies benevolence and is thereby able to lead others; he brings together what is excellent and is thereby able to accord with ritual propriety; he benefits things and is thereby able to harmonize righteousness; he is steadfast and firm and is thereby able to take charge of affairs. The gentleman practices these four virtues; hence it is said: ‘Qian: primal greatness, successful passage, benefit, and constancy.’”

Zhang Zhigao

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The Way of Qian is the highest teaching; these are the gentleman’s highest virtues. This composition elucidates them and deserves to be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: “Its language is sound and substantial, and its meaning clear and fully expressed. This is the work of someone deeply versed in the Book of Changes.”

Observe that the gentleman’s full realization of his nature proceeds from vigor, and the meaning of the words attached to Qian in the classic can be understood. For the completeness of the four virtues cannot be attained without the utmost vigor. Observing them in the gentleman, can one fail to understand the meaning of the classic’s words? The Commentary on the Words seems to say: The nature ordained by Heaven is present alike in all of us, but the achievement of fully realizing that nature belongs only to the gentleman. How does the gentleman fully realize his nature? The principle of primal greatness, as it exists in human beings, is benevolence. The gentleman preserves benevolence in his heart, and everything he puts into practice in his own person fully manifests the Way of benevolence. Thus, wherever his kindness and love reach, all things are gathered within [?]. Is this not sufficient to lead others? The principle of successful passage, as it exists in human beings, is ritual propriety. The gentleman uses ritual propriety to regulate his person [?], and everything he does in dealing with others brings together the established rites…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
通則秩敘以彰而稪皆中正矣不足以合禮乎
得利之理而爲義正天下之分以利其民君子
行而宜之之謂義也而質之無弗協矣得貞之
理而爲智明天下之理以守乎正君子知而弗
去之謂智也而動之爲有功矣夫君子行此四
者而所以行之者豈有他哉蓋其心本無私而
物不能屈故克全乎賦畀之重而於仁於禮盡
之而無歉也事爲有主而欲不能奪故不失乎
稟受之貞而於義於智全之而罔缺也君子非
===
健則四德其何以行之哉故曰乾元亨利貞乾
惟天下之至健也主宰造化而元亨利貞迭運
之不窮君子惟自強以法天也綱紀衆動而仁
禮義智兼體之不累然則君子一乾也而乾之
義非君子其孰明之噫天以至德命於人天之
未始不爲人也君子以全德配乎天人之未始
不爲天也易之理其至矣哉抑此王道也王道
本乎天德天德一誠而已誠則不貳不息故剛
健中正天德備而王道出也是故至誠贊天至
punctuated: 通，則秩敘以彰，而稪皆中正矣，不足以合禮乎？得利之理而爲義，正天下之分以利其民，君子行而宜之之謂義也，而質之無弗協矣。得貞之理而爲智，明天下之理以守乎正，君子知而弗去之謂智也，而動之爲有功矣。夫君子行此四者，而所以行之者豈有他哉？蓋其心本無私，而物不能屈，故克全乎賦畀之重，而於仁於禮盡之而無歉也；事爲有主，而欲不能奪，故不失乎稟受之貞，而於義於智全之而罔缺也。君子非健，則四德其何以行之哉？故曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」乾，惟天下之至健也，主宰造化，而元亨利貞迭運之不窮；君子惟自強以法天也，綱紀衆動，而仁禮義智兼體之不累。然則君子一乾也，而乾之義，非君子其孰明之？噫！天以至德命於人，天之未始不爲人也；君子以全德配乎天，人之未始不爲天也。《易》之理其至矣哉！抑此王道也。王道本乎天德，天德一誠而已。誠則不貳不息，故剛健中正，天德備而王道出也。是故至誠贊天，至
translation_en: …integration, so that ordered distinctions become manifest and all [actions?] attain centrality and correctness. Is this not sufficient to accord with ritual propriety? Apprehending the principle of benefit constitutes righteousness: the gentleman rectifies the distinctions throughout the world to benefit its people. His acting appropriately is what is called righteousness, and, when tested, nothing fails to accord with it. Apprehending the principle of constancy constitutes wisdom: the gentleman illuminates the principles of the world in order to hold fast to correctness. His knowing this and never departing from it is what is called wisdom, and his actions thus achieve results. Now, when the gentleman practices these four virtues, could there be any other means by which he practices them? His heart is fundamentally free of selfishness, and external things cannot bend him; thus he can fully preserve his weighty endowment and completely realize benevolence and ritual propriety without deficiency. His undertakings have a governing principle, and desires cannot wrest it away; thus he does not lose the rectitude of his received nature and fully realizes righteousness and wisdom without omission. Without vigor, how could the gentleman practice these four virtues? Hence it is said: “Qian: origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy.” Qian is the utmost vigor in the world. It governs creation and transformation, while origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy operate successively without end. The gentleman strengthens himself to model himself on Heaven. He orders his manifold actions and embodies benevolence, ritual propriety, righteousness, and wisdom together without encumbrance. Thus the gentleman is himself a Qian; who but the gentleman could elucidate the meaning of Qian? Ah! Heaven endows human beings with the highest virtue: Heaven has never been separate from humanity. The gentleman matches Heaven through complete virtue: humanity has never been separate from Heaven. How consummate are the principles of the Book of Changes! Indeed, this is the kingly Way. The kingly Way is rooted in Heaven’s virtue, and Heaven’s virtue is nothing but sincerity. Sincerity is undivided and unceasing; hence it is firm, vigorous, central, and correct. When Heaven’s virtue is complete, the kingly Way emerges. Therefore, utmost sincerity assists Heaven; utmost…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
聖如天惟大哉堯也君哉舜也然後能當之
言行君子之所以動天地也可不愼乎
沈存仁
考試官教諭陳　批　天人感通之理發得明透
可取
考試官教授吳　批　君子言行之愼其功在於
愼獨此作得之
大傳推言行感通之大而示人以致謹之意焉
蓋莫大於天地而言行感通之則言行之於人
===
重矣人其可以不致謹哉大傳釋中孚九二至
此若曰天人有感應之機乎誠爲昭格之本君
子欲存誠而妙感也亦致謹於言行而已矣彼
出身加民言之榮辱固徵諸民矣然言之理卽
天地之理也出之自我而天地之所視聽者在
焉發通見遠行之榮辱固徵諸遠矣然行之理
亦天地之理也所發在此而天地之所孚契者
存焉故未言也誠已格於上下由是言之則言
爲善言天地雖無言而於言之善者未始不歆
punctuated:
聖如天，惟大哉堯也，君哉舜也，然後能當之。

言行，君子之所以動天地也，可不愼乎？
沈存仁

考試官教諭陳批：天人感通之理，發得明透，可取。
考試官教授吳批：君子言行之愼，其功在於愼獨，此作得之。

大傳推言行感通之大，而示人以致謹之意焉。蓋莫大於天地，而言行感通之，則言行之於人重矣，人其可以不致謹哉？大傳釋中孚九二至此，若曰：天人有感應之機乎？誠爲昭格之本。君子欲存誠而妙感也，亦致謹於言行而已矣。彼出身加民，言之榮辱固徵諸民矣；然言之理卽天地之理也，出之自我，而天地之所視聽者在焉。發通見遠，行之榮辱固徵諸遠矣；然行之理亦天地之理也，所發在此，而天地之所孚契者存焉。故未言也，誠已格於上下；由是言之，則言爲善言，天地雖無言，而於言之善者未始不歆
translation_en:
…the supreme sage is like Heaven. Only Yao, of whom it was said, “Great indeed!”, and Shun, of whom it was said, “Truly a ruler!”, could merit this description.

“Words and deeds are the means by which the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth. Can he fail to be cautious?”
Shen Cunren

Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The principle of sympathetic communication between Heaven and humanity is expounded clearly and thoroughly. Worthy of acceptance.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “The gentleman’s caution in words and deeds depends upon his vigilance when alone. This composition grasps that point.”

The Great Commentary sets forth the far-reaching power of words and deeds to establish sympathetic communication, thereby showing people why they must exercise the utmost care. Nothing is greater than Heaven and Earth; yet words and deeds can establish sympathetic communication with them. Words and deeds thus carry great weight for human beings. How could anyone fail to exercise the utmost care?

At this point in its explanation of the second, yang line of the hexagram Zhongfu (Inner Sincerity), the Great Commentary seems to say: Is there a subtle mechanism of mutual response between Heaven and humanity? Sincerity is the foundation for reaching the divine. If the gentleman wishes to preserve sincerity and respond with wondrous efficacy, he need only exercise the utmost care in words and deeds. Words issue from his person and affect the people; the honor or disgrace they bring is certainly manifested among the people. Yet the principle governing words is precisely the principle of Heaven and Earth. They issue from oneself, but within them lies that to which Heaven and Earth attend with sight and hearing. Deeds issue forth, spread, and become manifest afar [?]; the honor or disgrace they bring is certainly manifested in distant places. Yet the principle governing deeds is likewise the principle of Heaven and Earth. They originate here, but within them lies that with which Heaven and Earth accord.

Thus, even before he speaks, his sincerity has already reached above and below. When he speaks on this basis, his words are good words. Though Heaven and Earth have no speech, they have never failed to take pleasure in words that are good…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
式昭夫至治之隆矣則德非徒具而政有成績
信可謂無虞也豈可不知所以保之哉蓋人情
鋭始而罔終也故必因其勤怠之分而加之以
懲戒之術人心樂成而難久也又必即其歌詠
之言以播之於律呂之間斯則激勸有道足以
起其奮迅不懈之心使勤者益樂於爲也怠者
亦勵其行也養道其永貞不替乎感發有機足
以堅其趨事順則之念使思其初者不流于佚
也樂其生者不倦于終也化理其恒久無弊乎
===
如此則克艱已盡無虞可保而伯益儆戒之旨
庶幾其無負矣帝當知所念哉抑愚於是而知
唐虞之治有所本矣蓋古今之論治惟敬與和
而已中庸自戒懼謹獨而推致於位育漢儒言
心和氣和而推極於天地之和應皆此意也故
愼憲欽哉之勑祗承儆戒之念篤恭之治也都
俞賡歌之風惟歌九歌之勸泰交之感也故曰
惟上下一於恭敬則天地自位萬物自育又曰
太和在唐虞宇宙間觀於此亦信
punctuated:
式昭夫至治之隆矣，則德非徒具而政有成績，信可謂無虞也，豈可不知所以保之哉？蓋人情鋭始而罔終也，故必因其勤怠之分而加之以懲戒之術；人心樂成而難久也，又必即其歌詠之言以播之於律呂之間。斯則激勸有道，足以起其奮迅不懈之心，使勤者益樂於爲也，怠者亦勵其行也，養道其永貞不替乎？感發有機，足以堅其趨事順則之念，使思其初者不流于佚也，樂其生者不倦于終也，化理其恒久無弊乎？如此則克艱已盡，無虞可保，而伯益儆戒之旨，庶幾其無負矣。帝當知所念哉！

抑愚於是而知唐虞之治有所本矣。蓋古今之論治，惟敬與和而已。《中庸》自戒懼謹獨而推致於位育，漢儒言心和氣和而推極於天地之和應，皆此意也。故「愼憲欽哉」之勑、祗承儆戒之念，篤恭之治也；都俞賡歌之風、惟歌九歌之勸，泰交之感也。故曰：「惟上下一於恭敬，則天地自位，萬物自育。」又曰：「太和在唐虞宇宙間。」觀於此亦信。
translation_en:
…thus manifesting the grandeur of perfect governance. Virtue is then more than merely possessed: government achieves results. This may truly be called freedom from care. How could one fail to understand how to preserve it? Human beings are keen at the outset but fail to persevere to the end. One must therefore apply methods of correction and admonition according to whether they are diligent or negligent. The human heart delights in accomplishment but finds it difficult to sustain its efforts. One must also take the words of their songs and set them to the musical pitches. With proper means of encouragement, one can arouse their vigorous and unflagging resolve, making the diligent take still greater pleasure in action and the negligent likewise exert themselves in their conduct. Would the way of nurturing [?] not then remain forever steadfast and undiminished? With effective means of stirring their feelings, one can strengthen their determination to attend to their duties and follow proper standards, so that those mindful of their beginnings do not lapse into ease, and those who delight in their lives do not tire before the end. Would transforming governance not then endure without deterioration? In this way, every effort to overcome difficulties will have been made, freedom from care can be preserved, and the intent of Bo Yi’s admonition will, one hopes, not have been betrayed. The emperor should know what to keep in mind!

Moreover, from this I, in my ignorance, understand that the governance of Tang and Yu had a foundation. Discussions of government, ancient and modern, come down to reverence and harmony alone. The Doctrine of the Mean proceeds from vigilance, apprehension, and care in solitude to Heaven and Earth taking their proper places and the myriad things receiving nourishment. Han Confucian scholars spoke of harmony of the heart and of vital energy, extending these ultimately to the harmonious response of Heaven and Earth. All express this same idea. Thus the injunction, “Be mindful of the statutes; be reverent,” and the resolve respectfully to receive admonition constitute governance through profound reverence. The practice of exchanging assent and continuing one another’s songs, together with the exhortation to sing the Nine Songs, embodies the mutual responsiveness of harmonious intercourse. Thus it is said: “When those above and below are united in reverence, Heaven and Earth will naturally take their proper places, and the myriad things will naturally receive nourishment.” It is also said: “Supreme harmony filled the universe in the age of Tang and Yu.” Considered in light of this, these words are indeed credible.

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
學古入官議事以制政乃不迷其爾典常
作之師
趙時雍
同考試官教諭馬　批詞氣不凡子亦博古通今
者
考試官教諭陳　批醇正之作
考試官教授吳　批清雅
賢王告庶官以酌古之益而尤欲其從今也夫
古法當酌而王制尤宜遵也合古今而用之治
===
道其無餘蘊乎成王訓迪百官之意若曰為治
者道固宜于遠宗法尤貴于近守凡我有官君
子當何如哉彼唐虞行帝道以著和盛之績夏
商行王道以垂用乂之休載籍猶存後世之成
法也爾庶官其尚學于入官之時前言往行必
多識焉而又因事參伍以酌其宜典謨訓誥必
遠稽焉而又隨事錯綜以盡其變則動有所徵
而經畫於朝廷者自恊乎弼亮之道謀非無據
而宣布於邦國者自得乎敷理之方尚何有于
punctuated:
「學古入官，議事以制，政乃不迷。其爾典常作之師。」
趙時雍
同考試官教諭馬　批：詞氣不凡，子亦博古通今者。
考試官教諭陳　批：醇正之作。
考試官教授吳　批：清雅。
賢王告庶官以酌古之益，而尤欲其從今也。夫古法當酌，而王制尤宜遵也。合古今而用之，治道其無餘蘊乎？成王訓迪百官之意若曰：為治者，道固宜于遠宗，法尤貴于近守。凡我有官君子，當何如哉？彼唐虞行帝道，以著和盛之績；夏商行王道，以垂用乂之休。載籍猶存，後世之成法也。爾庶官，其尚學于入官之時，前言往行必多識焉，而又因事參伍以酌其宜；典謨訓誥必遠稽焉，而又隨事錯綜以盡其變。則動有所徵，而經畫於朝廷者，自恊乎弼亮之道；謀非無據，而宣布於邦國者，自得乎敷理之方。尚何有于
translation_en:
“Study antiquity upon entering office; deliberate on affairs according to established rules, and government will not go astray. Take your enduring statutes and norms as your guide.”

Zhao Shiyong 趙時雍

Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: “The diction and spirit are extraordinary. You, too, are one who has extensive knowledge of antiquity and a thorough understanding of the present.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “A work of purity and rectitude.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “Lucid and elegant.”

The worthy king instructed the assembled officials in the benefits of weighing ancient precedents, yet wished above all that they should follow the institutions of their own day. Ancient laws should indeed be weighed, but the reigning king’s institutions should especially be obeyed. If antiquity and the present are combined in practice, would any profundity of the Way of government remain unexplored?

The intent of King Cheng’s instruction to the hundred officials was as though he said: “Those who govern should certainly look to the distant past as the source of the Way, yet in matters of law it is especially important to uphold the institutions close at hand. How, then, should all you gentlemen holding office under me conduct yourselves? Tang and Yu practiced the Way of the sage emperors, manifesting achievements of harmony and prosperity; Xia and Shang practiced the Way of kings, bequeathing the blessings of good government. Their written records still survive, providing established models for later generations. You assembled officials should therefore study upon entering office. You must acquaint yourselves widely with the words and deeds of the past, and further compare and examine them in relation to particular affairs to determine what is appropriate. You must investigate far back into the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements, and further draw upon them in varying combinations as affairs demand, to encompass every changing circumstance. Then your actions will have precedents to substantiate them, and your planning at court will naturally accord with the Way of assisting the ruler. Your deliberations will not lack foundations, and the measures you promulgate throughout the realm will naturally attain the proper method of extending good government. What room would there then be for …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
迷惑哉然學古固爲有獲而泥古未免違時其
必監于成憲而政令之敷施皆周官之所考定
也幸由舊章而事功之建立皆昭代之所垂憲
也官雖有治內治外之殊而所以亮天工者則
當遵王朝之度蓋我周之謨烈兼統帝王道莫
備焉者也而可或悖其啓佑之宏休哉職雖有
總治分治之殊而所以阜民物者則當師畫一
之規蓋我周之經制仰稽往聖法莫善焉者也
而可不守其燕翼之遺則哉夫酌古則有所考
===
而不失於自用矣從今則有所遵而不失於自
專矣古今咸備大猷允升爾有官君子其懋之
哉抑論治法雖有古今之異然二帝三王授受
一道夫苟得其心法之精則學古卽所以準今
一從周而堯舜禹湯之道具舉矣噫成王學懋
緝熈庶幾得乎心法者也以此爲訓亦有本哉
詩
以祈甘雨以介我稷黍以穀我士女
陸宗龍
punctuated:
迷惑哉？然學古固爲有獲，而泥古未免違時。其必監于成憲，而政令之敷施，皆周官之所考定也；幸由舊章，而事功之建立，皆昭代之所垂憲也。官雖有治內治外之殊，而所以亮天工者，則當遵王朝之度。蓋我周之謨烈，兼統帝王，道莫備焉者也，而可或悖其啓佑之宏休哉？職雖有總治分治之殊，而所以阜民物者，則當師畫一之規。蓋我周之經制，仰稽往聖，法莫善焉者也，而可不守其燕翼之遺則哉？夫酌古則有所考，而不失於自用矣；從今則有所遵，而不失於自專矣。古今咸備，大猷允升。爾有官君子，其懋之哉！抑論治法，雖有古今之異，然二帝三王授受一道。夫苟得其心法之精，則學古卽所以準今，一從周而堯舜禹湯之道具舉矣。噫！成王學懋緝熈，庶幾得乎心法者也。以此爲訓，亦有本哉！

詩
以祈甘雨，以介我稷黍，以穀我士女。
陸宗龍
translation_en:
…what confusion could remain? Yet although studying antiquity certainly brings benefits, clinging rigidly to antiquity inevitably conflicts with present circumstances. You must take established statutes as your guide, so that every governmental ordinance put into effect accords with what the officers of Zhou have examined and settled. Fortunately, by following the old regulations [?], all undertakings and achievements will accord with the precedents handed down by our illustrious dynasty. Although offices differ in administering affairs within and beyond the capital, those who assist Heaven’s work must follow the standards of the royal court. For the plans and achievements of our Zhou encompass those of both the ancient emperors and the kings: no Way is more complete. How could anyone contravene the magnificent beneficence by which they guide and aid posterity? Although responsibilities differ between overall and particular administration, those who enrich the people and foster all things must take uniform rules as their model. For the institutions of our Zhou look back to the sages of old: no laws are better. How could anyone fail to preserve the rules bequeathed for the peace and protection of descendants? By weighing antiquity, one has evidence to consult and avoids the error of trusting only oneself; by following the present, one has standards to obey and avoids the error of acting on one’s own authority. With past and present both fully provided for, the great Way of government will assuredly flourish. You gentlemen who hold office, exert yourselves!

Yet, when discussing methods of government, although antiquity and the present differ, the Two Emperors and the Three Kings transmitted and received a single Way. If one grasps the essence of their teaching of the mind, studying antiquity is precisely the means of conforming to the present. By following Zhou alone, the Ways of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang are all put into practice. Ah! King Cheng diligently pursued learning and continued to attain ever greater illumination; he came close to grasping this teaching of the mind. In making this his admonition, he indeed had a foundation!

Book of Odes
“To pray for timely rain, to aid our millet crops, and to nourish our men and women.”
Lu Zonglong.

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭陳　批〔用意周匝措詞典雅可以〕
〔觀所蘊矣〕
考試官教授吳　批〔公卿重農之意宛然在目〕
公卿之祈年而擾天以惠民焉蓋民非黍稷弗
養也然必資於天澤焉此公卿所以爲民祈之
也歟詩述公卿有田祿者力農奉祭而作至此
意曰我公卿之重農凡以爲民也是故當報典
之告成而遂有祈年之舉者豈無爲哉蓋苗生
資於雨而降雨在於天此民之不能自致而仰
===
望於神者也今作樂以御之也庶其感通於和
樂之來時雨降焉此疆彼界均霑夫優渥之仁
昭格於冥漠之中靈雨零焉中公外私咸溥夫
霑足之惠天時有生斯地利有養也土膏沃而
物生遂黍稷時見其庭碩矣天有顯惠斯人有
全功也滋培厚而物性充黍稷時見其堅好矣
由是收成富而百室既盈斂穫多而民人胥育
以之引養以之引恬蒸民遂乃粒之休而阻饑
其可免焉則神之降康於吾民亦既溥矣謂非
punctuated:
考試官教諭陳，批〔用意周匝，措詞典雅，可以觀所蘊矣。〕
考試官教授吳，批〔公卿重農之意，宛然在目。〕
公卿之祈年，而擾天以惠民焉。蓋民非黍稷弗養也，然必資於天澤焉，此公卿所以爲民祈之也歟！詩述公卿有田祿者力農奉祭而作，至此，意曰：我公卿之重農，凡以爲民也。是故當報典之告成，而遂有祈年之舉者，豈無爲哉？蓋苗生資於雨，而降雨在於天，此民之不能自致而仰望於神者也。今作樂以御之也，庶其感通於和樂之來，時雨降焉，此疆彼界，均霑夫優渥之仁；昭格於冥漠之中，靈雨零焉，中公外私，咸溥夫霑足之惠。天時有生，斯地利有養也，土膏沃而物生遂，黍稷時見其庭碩矣。天有顯惠，斯人有全功也，滋培厚而物性充，黍稷時見其堅好矣。由是收成富而百室既盈，斂穫多而民人胥育，以之引養，以之引恬，蒸民遂乃粒之休，而阻饑其可免焉。則神之降康於吾民，亦既溥矣，謂非
translation_en:
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔The conception is comprehensive and the wording classically elegant; these reveal the learning he possesses.〕
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔The concern of the dukes and ministers for agriculture is vividly present before our eyes.〕
The dukes and ministers pray for a bountiful year, importuning Heaven [?] to benefit the people. The people cannot be nourished without millet, yet millet necessarily depends upon Heaven’s beneficent moisture. Is this not why the dukes and ministers offer prayers on the people’s behalf? This poem in the Book of Odes was composed to describe how dukes and ministers who receive landed emoluments devote themselves to agriculture and perform sacrifices. At this point its meaning is: We dukes and ministers value agriculture entirely for the people’s sake. Thus, when the rites of thanksgiving are completed, we proceed to pray for a bountiful year. Could this be without purpose?
For seedlings depend upon rain to grow, and the sending of rain rests with Heaven. This is something the people cannot obtain by their own efforts, and for which they look up to the spirits. Now music is performed to welcome them, in the hope that the harmonious music will move them to respond and timely rain will descend, so that every field and boundary alike receives this abundant benevolence. May our sincerity reach them in their unseen realm, so that numinous rain falls and the public fields at the center and private fields surrounding them all receive ample moisture.
When Heaven’s seasons bring forth life, the earth’s resources provide nourishment. The soil is rich and moist, and growing things flourish; in due season the millet appears tall and luxuriant [?]. When Heaven bestows manifest bounty, human efforts achieve their full result. With abundant nourishment and cultivation, growing things realize their nature fully; in due season the millet appears firm and fine. Thus the harvest is plentiful and the households’ granaries are filled; much is gathered in, and all the people are nourished. Through this their sustenance and tranquility are prolonged. The multitude enjoys the blessing of grain to eat and can escape the distress of hunger. The well-being that the spirits bestow upon our people is thus far-reaching indeed. To say that it is not…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
商人伐楚必述遠人之守禮者以責之也夫禮
行於商不以遠而可違也商人舉氐羌以聲責
楚之罪也宜哉殷武祀高宗之樂也此則述責
楚之辭若曰王治極於無外王師征乎不庭爾
荊楚之敢於稱叛也獨不聞我商先世之所以
服遠者乎誠以我祖成湯之在昔也王靈丕振
而遐邇同風聖武孔昭而華夷一統雖遠如氐
羌政敎不加初未必其來享也然仰戴乎寬仁
之主自願輸夫納款之忱凡夫任土作貢而不
敢自私者若有所以驅之也正朔不及初未必
其來王也然向慕乎彰信之風自莫已其朝宗
之念凡夫稱臣請命而不敢自專者若有所以
聯之也其心蓋曰以內馭外者王者之威以夷
事華者吾人之分享以方物非自今伊始也蓋
由商之常禮以脩吾之常儀所以明有尊也否
則是自干後至之誅矣而可乎王以求章非於
今爲然也蓋率商之常制以盡吾之常職所以
明有分也否則是自蹈犯順之罪矣而可乎夫
punctuated: 商人伐楚，必述遠人之守禮者以責之也。夫禮行於商，不以遠而可違也。商人舉氐羌以聲責楚之罪也，宜哉！《殷武》，祀高宗之樂也。此則述責楚之辭，若曰：王治極於無外，王師征乎不庭。爾荊楚之敢於稱叛也，獨不聞我商先世之所以服遠者乎？誠以我祖成湯之在昔也，王靈丕振，而遐邇同風；聖武孔昭，而華夷一統。雖遠如氐羌，政敎不加，初未必其來享也，然仰戴乎寬仁之主，自願輸夫納款之忱。凡夫任土作貢而不敢自私者，若有所以驅之也。正朔不及，初未必其來王也，然向慕乎彰信之風，自莫已其朝宗之念。凡夫稱臣請命而不敢自專者，若有所以聯之也。其心蓋曰：以內馭外者，王者之威；以夷事華者，吾人之分。享以方物，非自今伊始也，蓋由商之常禮，以脩吾之常儀，所以明有尊也。否則是自干後至之誅矣，而可乎？王以求章，非於今爲然也，蓋率商之常制，以盡吾之常職，所以明有分也。否則是自蹈犯順之罪矣，而可乎？夫
translation_en:
When the people of Shang attacked Chu, they necessarily invoked the observance of ritual by distant peoples to rebuke it. For the rites prevailing under Shang could not be transgressed on the grounds of distance. How fitting that the people of Shang should cite the Di and Qiang to proclaim Chu’s guilt! “Martial Shang” (Yin wu) is music for sacrifices to Gaozong. This passage recounts the words reproaching Chu, as though saying: The king’s governance extends everywhere, leaving nothing outside it; the king’s armies campaign against those who fail to attend his court. You of Jingchu dare to rebel—have you alone not heard how our Shang forebears brought distant peoples into submission?

Indeed, in the time of our ancestor Cheng Tang, royal majesty spread mightily, and near and far shared the same customs; sagely martial power shone brilliantly, and the Hua and Yi were united under one rule. Even peoples as distant as the Di and Qiang, beyond the reach of government and instruction, were not initially certain to come bearing offerings. Yet, looking up in allegiance to a generous and benevolent lord, they willingly expressed their sincere submission. All who presented tribute according to their lands’ produce, daring not to keep it for themselves, seemed impelled by something. Beyond the reach of the royal calendar, they were not initially certain to come and acknowledge the king. Yet, admiring his manifest trustworthiness, they could not restrain their desire to attend his court. All who declared themselves his subjects and sought his commands, daring not to act on their own authority, seemed bound to him by something.

In their hearts they presumably said: To govern the outer regions from the center is the king’s authority; to serve the Hua as Yi is our allotted duty. Presenting local products as offerings did not begin only today. We follow Shang’s enduring rites to perform our customary ceremonies, thereby making clear that there is a superior whom we honor. Otherwise, we would bring upon ourselves the punishment for arriving late—how could that be permissible? Coming to acknowledge the king and seeking distinction [?] is not something done only now. We follow Shang’s enduring institutions to discharge our regular duties, thereby making clear the distinctions of rank. Otherwise, we would ourselves incur the guilt of defying the proper order—how could that be permissible? Now …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
觀氏羗之享則享於荊楚可知也觀氏羗之王
則王於荊楚可知也以先世所臣之國而不臣
於今其能逭於撻伐之加乎吁高宗責楚之義
嚴矣抑高宗亦不專恃乎此也觀夫恭默思道
德懋於巳矣不僭不濫政制其中矣而又得良
弼之賚以爲之輔焉此所以撻武而楚自服也
此所以能纘湯緒而成中興之烈也商人世世
祀之也固宜
春秋
===
秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀僖公三
年
陳時言
同考試官教諭謝 批 善發明經傳本旨而詞亦
簡嚴可錄
考試官教諭陳 批 其旨瑩其詞文
考試官教授吳 批 筆力謹嚴
春秋於伯主善其講好以定制外之謀焉夫謀
定而後戰者勝也此齊桓之會陽穀所以善於
punctuated:
觀氏羗之享，則享於荊楚可知也；觀氏羗之王，則王於荊楚可知也。以先世所臣之國而不臣於今，其能逭於撻伐之加乎？吁！高宗責楚之義嚴矣！抑高宗亦不專恃乎此也。觀夫恭默思道，德懋於巳矣；不僭不濫，政制其中矣；而又得良弼之賚，以爲之輔焉。此所以撻武而楚自服也，此所以能纘湯緒而成中興之烈也。商人世世祀之也，固宜。
春秋
秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。僖公三年。
陳時言
同考試官教諭謝批：善發明經傳本旨，而詞亦簡嚴，可錄。
考試官教諭陳批：其旨瑩，其詞文。
考試官教授吳批：筆力謹嚴。
春秋於伯主，善其講好以定制外之謀焉。夫謀定而後戰者勝也，此齊桓之會陽穀所以善於
translation_en:
…From the tribute offered by the Di and Qiang [?], we may understand that tribute was also required of Jingchu; from the attendance of the Di and Qiang at the royal court, we may understand that Jingchu too was required to attend. If they would not now acknowledge as sovereign the state their forebears had served, could they escape punitive attack? Ah! How exacting was the righteousness with which Gaozong called Chu to account! Yet Gaozong did not rely exclusively upon this. Consider how, reverent and silent, he contemplated the Way, cultivating virtue within himself. Neither erring in rewards nor excessive in punishments, he brought government into due balance. Moreover, he received the gift of an excellent minister to assist him. This was why he could display his martial might and Chu would submit of its own accord. This was why he could carry on Tang’s legacy and accomplish the great work of restoring the dynasty. It was indeed fitting that the people of Shang should offer sacrifices to him generation after generation.
Spring and Autumn Annals
“In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu.” Third year of Duke Xi.
Chen Shiyan
Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: “He ably elucidates the original purport of the classic and its commentary, and his language is also concise and exact. Worth selecting.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “His meaning is lucid; his language is elegant.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “His writing is careful and disciplined.”
In its treatment of hegemonic lords, the Spring and Autumn Annals commends their cultivation of friendly relations to settle plans for keeping external powers in check. Those who settle their plans before going to war are victorious. This is why Duke Huan of Qi’s meeting at Yanggu was effective in…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
制楚也歟且伯有攘夷之責必禦之於其來而
武有制勝之經必謀之於其豫君子所以善夫
陽穀之會者何也蓋荊楚爲大邦之仇所以問
猾夏之罪義莫有先焉者也齊桓當圖伯之始
所以挫强楚之鋒事莫有難焉者也使不定謀
於先則在我者雖有言可執何以抗夫方張之
勢在彼者雖有罪可聲何以啓夫服義之忱於
是務離其黨藏戰伐於申好之中玉帛之交錯
其折衝之勝算乎豫結其援寓神武於敦睦之
===
内壇坫之周旋其攻心之上策乎慮夫楚之進
焉無以當其鋭也則命八國厚集其陳以振撻
伐之威聚而爲正敵不知所以攻吾之堅矣慮
夫楚之退焉無以躡其後也則命江黄各守其
境以爲犄角之助分而爲奇敵不知所以窺吾
之秘矣算之多者其事易成不待夫侵蔡次陘
之日而可以策必勝之道勢之孤者其强易弱
雖有乎方城漢水之險而無以敵萬全之師桓
之善於制楚也固如此哉屈完盟而楚人輸款
punctuated: 制楚也歟？且伯有攘夷之責，必禦之於其來；而武有制勝之經，必謀之於其豫。君子所以善夫陽穀之會者何也？蓋荊楚爲大邦之仇，所以問猾夏之罪，義莫有先焉者也。齊桓當圖伯之始，所以挫强楚之鋒，事莫有難焉者也。使不定謀於先，則在我者雖有言可執，何以抗夫方張之勢？在彼者雖有罪可聲，何以啓夫服義之忱？於是務離其黨，藏戰伐於申好之中。玉帛之交錯，其折衝之勝算乎？豫結其援，寓神武於敦睦之内。壇坫之周旋，其攻心之上策乎？慮夫楚之進焉，無以當其鋭也，則命八國厚集其陳，以振撻伐之威。聚而爲正，敵不知所以攻吾之堅矣。慮夫楚之退焉，無以躡其後也，則命江黄各守其境，以爲犄角之助。分而爲奇，敵不知所以窺吾之秘矣。算之多者，其事易成，不待夫侵蔡次陘之日，而可以策必勝之道；勢之孤者，其强易弱，雖有乎方城漢水之險，而無以敵萬全之師。桓之善於制楚也，固如此哉！屈完盟，而楚人輸款
translation_en: …in restraining Chu? Moreover, a hegemon bears responsibility for repelling the non-Chinese peoples and must resist their advance; warfare has principles for securing victory, and plans must be laid beforehand. Why do gentlemen commend the meeting at Yanggu? Jing-Chu was an enemy of the great states: in terms of righteousness, nothing took precedence over calling it to account for its crime of disturbing the Chinese states. When Duke Huan of Qi was first seeking hegemony, no undertaking was more difficult than blunting the spearhead of mighty Chu. Had he not settled his plans beforehand, then, although we possessed grounds to uphold our case, how could we have resisted its burgeoning power? Although its crimes could be proclaimed, how could we have awakened in it a sincere willingness to submit to righteousness? Thus he sought to detach its allies, concealing preparations for war within the renewal of friendly relations. Was not the exchange of jade and silk a winning calculation for overcoming the enemy? He secured support in advance, lodging awe-inspiring martial power within the strengthening of amity. Were not the diplomatic exchanges at ceremonial altars and stands a supreme strategy for winning hearts? Concerned that, should Chu advance, there would be no means of withstanding its onslaught, he ordered the eight states to mass their formations in strength, displaying the might of a punitive expedition. Concentrated, they constituted the regular force, and the enemy could not discover how to attack our solid defenses. Concerned that, should Chu retreat, there would be no means of pursuing it, he ordered Jiang and Huang each to guard its own territory, providing mutually supporting positions. Dispersed, they constituted the extraordinary force, and the enemy could not discover how to fathom our hidden dispositions. Those whose calculations are ample readily accomplish their undertakings: even before the day of the incursion into Cai and the encampment at Xing, the course to certain victory could be determined. Those whose position is isolated readily pass from strength to weakness: even with the natural defenses of Fangcheng and the Han River, they could not withstand an army prepared for every eventuality. Such indeed was Duke Huan’s skill in restraining Chu! Qu Wan entered into a covenant, and the people of Chu tendered their allegiance…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
之恐後春秋末言以善之宜矣抑是舉也桓謀
之仲相之念深慮周圖回於齊國之上追其旣
也兵不暴而志不驕亦庶幾乎王者之事矣然
又有轅濤塗之執何也噫桓德於是乎衰矣仲
尼之徒無道桓文之事者以此
齊人歸我濟西田宣公十年齊人來歸鄆
讙龜陰田定公十年
陳揚產
同考試官教諭謝　批　歸田一也而其情則殊予
能發之足以立勸懲之準矣
考試官教諭陳　批　得聖人書法之意
考試官教授吳　批　詞嚴義正
春秋兩著歸地者之情異而褒貶之法立矣夫
齊人歸地於魯雖同而歸之之情則異也春秋
得不寓意以褒貶之哉且濟西魯田也自魯宣
賂齊而齊之有濟西也久矣茲曷爲而歸魯耶
蓋平州會而負逆於己懼討於人斯宣公之志
也故婚好之結於齊朝聘之勤於齊所以順而
punctuated:
之恐後，《春秋》末言以善之，宜矣。抑是舉也，桓謀之，仲相之，念深慮周，圖回於齊國之上。追其旣也，兵不暴而志不驕，亦庶幾乎王者之事矣。然又有轅濤塗之執，何也？噫！桓德於是乎衰矣。仲尼之徒無道桓文之事者，以此。
「齊人歸我濟西田。」宣公十年。「齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。」定公十年。
陳揚產
同考試官教諭謝，批：「歸田一也，而其情則殊，予能發之，足以立勸懲之準矣。」
考試官教諭陳，批：「得聖人書法之意。」
考試官教授吳，批：「詞嚴義正。」
《春秋》兩著歸地者之情異，而褒貶之法立矣。夫齊人歸地於魯雖同，而歸之之情則異也，《春秋》得不寓意以褒貶之哉？且濟西，魯田也。自魯宣賂齊，而齊之有濟西也久矣。茲曷爲而歸魯耶？蓋平州會，而負逆於己，懼討於人，斯宣公之志也。故婚好之結於齊，朝聘之勤於齊，所以順而
translation_en:
…fearing to be last in offering allegiance. It was fitting that the concluding words of the Spring and Autumn Annals should commend this [?]. In this undertaking, Duke Huan planned and Zhong assisted him; their thinking was profound and their deliberations comprehensive as they devised their strategy at the court of Qi. Looking back upon its completion, the troops had not acted brutally, nor had ambition turned to arrogance: this came close to the conduct of a true king. Yet why was there also the arrest of Yuan Taotu? Alas! Here Duke Huan’s virtue declined. This is why the followers of Zhongni did not speak of the deeds of Dukes Huan and Wen.
“The men of Qi returned to us the lands west of the Ji River.” Tenth year of Duke Xuan. “The men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” Tenth year of Duke Ding.
Chen Yangchan
Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: “The return of land is the same in both cases, but the underlying motives differ. I can elucidate this [?], sufficiently to establish a standard for encouragement and admonition.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “It grasps the Sage’s intent in his manner of recording events.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: “The language is stern and the principles upright.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals twice makes clear the differing motives of those who returned land, thereby establishing its method of praise and blame. Although both instances involved the men of Qi returning land to Lu, the motives behind the returns differed. Could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to convey its judgment through praise and blame? Now, the lands west of the Ji River belonged to Lu. Ever since Duke Xuan of Lu had used them to bribe Qi, Qi had held them for a long time. Why, then, were they now returned to Lu? At the meeting at Pingzhou, Duke Xuan bore the guilt of rebellion and feared a punitive attack by others: such was his state of mind. Hence he established marriage ties with Qi and assiduously paid court visits and sent diplomatic missions to Qi, doing all this in order to submit and…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
事之者至矣齊則以其娟乎已者爲可悅而不
以其悖乎倫者爲可誅始之取非其有今之歸
不以道刑惡之典不加而怡然惠愛以相遺司
馬之法不請而懽然土地之授受由是宣公得
以安其位魯人無以議其惡而大防潰矣謂非
濟西之歸有以成之耶春秋書曰歸我所以惡
夫親我者而惠公之罪著矣若鄆讙龜陰亦魯
田也自魯人失守而齊之有三田也舊矣玆曷
爲而歸魯耶蓋夾谷會而謀不行於犂彌聽不
===
惑於景公斯孔子之化也故語以華夏之盟好
昭以神人之德義所以導而諭之者切矣齊則
悟其夷俗之爲陋而翻然以古道爲可行數世
所侵之地返之壇坫之上野享不設既以率禮
之正而謝過以質又有格心之孚是蓋晏子得
以效其忠景公有以成其美而大化昭矣謂非
三田之歸有以得之耶春秋書曰來歸所以見
夫歸之誠而景公之善彰矣夫歸地一也有出
於濟惡而歸之者則其事爲貶有本於感化而
punctuated: 事之者至矣。齊則以其娟乎已者爲可悅，而不以其悖乎倫者爲可誅。始之取，非其有；今之歸，不以道。刑惡之典不加，而怡然惠愛以相遺；司馬之法不請，而懽然土地之授受。由是宣公得以安其位，魯人無以議其惡，而大防潰矣。謂非濟西之歸有以成之耶？春秋書曰：「歸我。」所以惡夫親我者，而惠公之罪著矣。若鄆、讙、龜陰，亦魯田也。自魯人失守，而齊之有三田也舊矣。玆曷爲而歸魯耶？蓋夾谷會，而謀不行於犂彌，聽不惑於景公，斯孔子之化也。故語以華夏之盟好，昭以神人之德義，所以導而諭之者切矣。齊則悟其夷俗之爲陋，而翻然以古道爲可行。數世所侵之地，返之壇坫之上。野享不設，既以率禮之正；而謝過以質，又有格心之孚。是蓋晏子得以效其忠，景公有以成其美，而大化昭矣。謂非三田之歸有以得之耶？春秋書曰：「來歸。」所以見夫歸之誠，而景公之善彰矣。夫歸地一也，有出於濟惡而歸之者，則其事爲貶；有本於感化而
translation_en:
…had gone to the utmost in serving Qi. Qi took pleasure in his ingratiating conduct toward itself [?], but did not consider his violation of the moral order worthy of punishment. At first it took what did not belong to it; now it returned it without regard for the Way. The statutes for punishing evil were not applied; instead, favors were cheerfully bestowed. The military law of the Minister of War was not invoked; instead, territory was happily handed over and received. Thus Duke Xuan was able to secure his position, the people of Lu had no means of censuring his wickedness, and the great moral barrier collapsed. Can one say that the return of Jixi did not help bring this about? The Spring and Autumn Annals records: “Returned to us.” This condemns the one who favored us, and thus makes Duke Hui’s guilt manifest.

As for Yun, Huan, and Guiyin, these too were lands of Lu. Ever since the people of Lu failed to hold them, Qi had long possessed these three territories. Why, then, did it now return them to Lu? At the meeting at Jiagu, Li Mi’s scheme was not put into effect, and Duke Jing was not misled by what he heard: this was the transforming influence of Confucius. Confucius spoke to him of the bonds of alliance among the states of Huaxia and made clear the virtue and righteousness upheld by spirits and men. His guidance and instruction were earnest indeed. Qi then recognized the baseness of its barbarian customs and promptly came to see that the ancient Way could be practiced. Lands encroached upon over several generations were restored at the diplomatic altar. By foregoing a banquet in the open country, Qi conformed to correct ritual; by apologizing for its faults with sincerity, it further showed the good faith of a heart that had been set right. Thus Yanzi was able to demonstrate his loyalty, Duke Jing was able to bring his good qualities to fruition, and the great transforming influence became manifest. Can one say that the return of the three territories did not help achieve this? The Spring and Autumn Annals records: “Came to return.” This reveals the sincerity of the return and makes Duke Jing’s goodness manifest.

Returning territory is, in itself, the same act. When someone returns it to abet wrongdoing, the deed merits condemnation; when the return stems from moral transformation and…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
歸之者則其事爲褒春秋之立義精矣抑齊惠
不足言也景公以歷階數語良心動而侵疆復
亦若可與有爲矣而女樂之饋又何爲者耶卒
使夫子之不究其用也豈非天之未欲平治天
下乎吁良可慨已

所習成於教也道德一矣俗其有不同於下乎
記王制者之意若曰先王立鄉學而以司徒總
其政令也其廸乎民者甚備其範乎民者甚詳
豈特禮教與政而已哉彼人所共由之謂道天
下無異道也則以其所共由者繹而明之以布
punctuated:
歸之者，則其事爲褒。春秋之立義精矣！抑齊惠不足言也，景公以歷階數語，良心動而侵疆復，亦若可與有爲矣。而女樂之饋，又何爲者耶？卒使夫子之不究其用也，豈非天之未欲平治天下乎？吁，良可慨已！
《禮記》
一道德以同俗。
胡夢豸
同考試官學正陳批：發揮化民成俗之意透徹，錄之。
考試官教諭陳批：詞明暢而意雋永。
考試官教授吳批：善體認發揮。
大臣教民鄉學，必有所以同乎其習也。蓋民之所習成於教也，道德一矣，俗其有不同於下乎？記王制者之意若曰：先王立鄉學，而以司徒總其政令也。其廸乎民者甚備，其範乎民者甚詳，豈特禮教與政而已哉？彼人所共由之謂道，天下無異道也，則以其所共由者繹而明之，以布
translation_en:
…when the land is returned as a result of moral transformation, the deed merits praise. How subtle are the judgments established by the Spring and Autumn Annals! Yet Duke Hui of Qi scarcely deserves discussion. As for Duke Jing, a few words spoken upon ascending the steps stirred his conscience, and he restored the territory he had seized. He, too, seemed someone with whom something worthwhile might be accomplished. Yet what was the purpose of his gift of female musicians? In the end, it prevented the Master from fully putting his abilities to use. Was this not because Heaven did not yet wish to bring peace and good government to the world? Alas, this is truly lamentable!
Record of Rites
“Unify the Way and virtue in order to make customs alike.”
Hu Mengzhi
Associate Examiner Chen, School Director, comments: “Thoroughly elucidates the meaning of transforming the people and establishing customs. Include it.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The language is clear and fluent, and the meaning rich and enduring.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “Shows a fine grasp of the meaning and develops it well.”
When a great minister teaches the people in local schools, he must have a means of making their habits alike. For the habits of the people are formed through instruction. Once the Way and virtue are unified, could customs among the people below fail to be alike? The intent of the author of the ‘Royal Regulations’ chapter seems to be this: the former kings established local schools and placed the Minister of Education in overall charge of their administrative directives. Their guidance of the people was comprehensive, and the standards they set for the people were detailed. How could these have been limited to ritual instruction and government alone? That which all people follow in common is called the Way; there are no different Ways in the world. Thus, what all follow in common is expounded and clarified, so as to promulgate it…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
於章程之內人所同得之謂德天下無異德也
則以其所同得者揭而示之以昭於品式之中
皇極大中之矩吾爲之匡直之以成其能焉智
不能益愚不能損也而道如此乎其一矣天命
人心之正吾爲之輔翼之以勵其趨焉賢不能
過不肖不能不及也而德如此乎其一矣若是
者正所以示之軌儀則天下之趨向一焉曉然
知教於上者之可從而不可悖也莫不師資以
自守導之指歸則天下之習尚同焉昭然知訓
===
於上者之可守而不可違也莫不觀法以自淑
雖曰五方各有性也然師無異教則涵濡久而
向方同蓋渾乎一其禮教之守而無有家自爲
說者矣雖曰千里不同風也然教無異指則觀
感深而遷善速蓋蕩乎一其政教之遵而無有
人自爲學者矣卿大夫以之治其國者此道此
德也士庶人以之治其身者此道此德也何莫
不本於司徒之善教乎抑一道德以同俗固司
徒之教而古者比屋可封之治於是乎可稽矣
punctuated: 於章程之內。人所同得之謂德，天下無異德也，則以其所同得者揭而示之，以昭於品式之中。皇極大中之矩，吾爲之匡直之，以成其能焉，智不能益，愚不能損也，而道如此乎其一矣。天命人心之正，吾爲之輔翼之，以勵其趨焉，賢不能過，不肖不能不及也，而德如此乎其一矣。若是者，正所以示之軌儀，則天下之趨向一焉，曉然知教於上者之可從而不可悖也，莫不師資以自守；導之指歸，則天下之習尚同焉，昭然知訓於上者之可守而不可違也，莫不觀法以自淑。雖曰五方各有性也，然師無異教，則涵濡久而向方同，蓋渾乎一其禮教之守，而無有家自爲說者矣。雖曰千里不同風也，然教無異指，則觀感深而遷善速，蓋蕩乎一其政教之遵，而無有人自爲學者矣。卿大夫以之治其國者，此道此德也；士庶人以之治其身者，此道此德也。何莫不本於司徒之善教乎？抑一道德以同俗，固司徒之教，而古者比屋可封之治，於是乎可稽矣。
translation_en:
…within the established regulations. What people receive in common is called virtue. There is no different virtue anywhere under Heaven; therefore, what they receive in common is set forth and shown to them, making it manifest in the prescribed standards. As for the rule of the august ultimate and the great mean, I rectify and guide the people by it, bringing their capacities to fulfillment. The wise cannot add to it, nor can the foolish diminish it: thus is the Way made one. As for the rectitude of Heaven’s mandate and the human heart, I support and assist the people in it, encouraging their progress toward it. The worthy cannot exceed it, nor may the unworthy fall short of it: thus is virtue made one.

Such measures precisely serve to show people the proper patterns of conduct, so that all under Heaven share one direction. Clearly understanding that instruction from above is to be followed and must not be opposed, all take it as their teacher and guide in maintaining their conduct. These measures direct people toward their proper goal, so that customary practices throughout the realm become alike. Clearly understanding that admonitions from above are to be upheld and must not be transgressed, all look to them as models for improving themselves.

Although it is said that the people of the five regions each have their own dispositions, when teachers do not differ in their teachings, prolonged immersion in their influence brings people to face the same direction. Their observance of ritual instruction is thereby thoroughly unified, and no household devises a doctrine of its own. Although it is said that customs differ across a thousand li, when instruction does not differ in its purport, the influence of observed examples penetrates deeply, and people turn swiftly toward goodness. Their adherence to government and instruction is thereby broadly unified, and no individual pursues a teaching of his own.

It is this Way and this virtue that ministers and grandees employ to govern their states; it is this Way and this virtue that men of service and commoners employ to govern themselves. How could any of this fail to be rooted in the excellent instruction of the Minister of Education? Indeed, unifying the Way and virtue so as to make customs alike is precisely the instruction of the Minister of Education. Here we may discern the basis of that ancient good order in which every household had someone worthy of enfeoffment.

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
後世言道以黃老言治以申韓而百氏競興又
奚望乎道德之一風俗之同哉董子謂春秋大
一統庶有合於一道德之旨而程子以爲有儒
者氣象詎不信夫
是故先王慎所以感之者故禮以道其志
樂以和其聲政以一其行刑以防其姦
禮樂刑政其極一也所以同民心而出
治道也
吳道東
===
同考試官學正陳　批　王者感人有道此作得之
考試官教諭陳　批　明粹可錄
考試官教授吳　批　精純典雅獨超諸作
佳士也
記者詳先王慎政以感人而必申其意焉夫禮
樂刑政先王以之感人而慎者也謂非所以成
天下之化而何哉記樂記者之意蓋謂情動於
物音之所由生也政出於上情之所自制也是
故先王以在民者不能已其應物之感而在我
punctuated:
後世言道以黃老，言治以申韓，而百氏競興，又奚望乎道德之一、風俗之同哉？董子謂《春秋》大一統，庶有合於一道德之旨，而程子以爲有儒者氣象，詎不信夫！

是故先王慎所以感之者，故禮以道其志，樂以和其聲，政以一其行，刑以防其姦。禮樂刑政，其極一也，所以同民心而出治道也。

吳道東

同考試官學正陳　批：王者感人有道，此作得之。
考試官教諭陳　批：明粹可錄。
考試官教授吳　批：精純典雅，獨超諸作，佳士也。

記者詳先王慎政以感人，而必申其意焉。夫禮樂刑政，先王以之感人而慎者也，謂非所以成天下之化而何哉？記《樂記》者之意，蓋謂情動於物，音之所由生也；政出於上，情之所自制也。是故先王以在民者不能已其應物之感，而在我
translation_en:
In later ages, those who spoke of the Way relied on Huang-Lao teachings, and those who spoke of government relied on Shen Buhai and Han Fei. With the hundred schools competing to arise, how could one still hope for unity in the Way and virtue, and uniformity in customs? Master Dong held that the Spring and Autumn Annals exalts comprehensive unity; this comes close to the purpose of unifying the Way and virtue. Master Cheng considered him to possess the bearing of a Confucian scholar. Is this not indeed true!

“For this reason, the former kings were careful about the means by which they influenced the people. Thus ritual guided their aspirations, music harmonized their voices, government unified their conduct, and punishments prevented their wrongdoing. Ritual, music, punishments, and government have a single ultimate aim: to unite the hearts of the people and bring forth the way of good government.”

Wu Daodong

Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor, comments: “There is a proper way for a king to influence people; this composition grasps it.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Clear and refined; worthy of inclusion.”
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “Precise, pure, classically elegant, and uniquely surpassing the other compositions. A fine scholar indeed.”

The recorder explains in detail how the former kings exercised care in government in order to influence people, and insists on elaborating the meaning. Ritual, music, punishments, and government were the means by which the former kings influenced people, and in which they exercised care. If these were not the means of completing the moral transformation of all under Heaven, what else could they be? The intention of the compiler of the Record of Music was surely to say that feelings are stirred by external things, and this is how sounds arise; government issues from above, and this is how feelings are regulated. Therefore, the former kings considered that the people could not restrain their emotional responses to external things, while what lay with themselves …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
者所當慎其動衆之原志也聲也民之感於物
而未化於物也則有以養之以禮道志以樂和
聲所以培其本然之善者其道蓋詳於上矣行
也姦也民之誘於物而將流於邪也則有以閑
之以政一行以刑防姦所以禁其將萌之惡者
其道蓋豫於先矣是禮與樂不一其事而施之
於民則各神乎鼓舞之用政與刑不同其道而
推之於下則均妙乎化導之方若此者何哉蓋
示之觀感以約其趨善同好也不善同惡也會
于其極而其心一焉則不怨不爭强弱之所以
各安其分也而道化於是乎宣布矣納之範圍
以聯其志過思抑也不及思企也協于其中而
其心一焉則合愛合敬智愚之所以各得其所
也而德教於是乎流行矣民心旣同治道不從
是而出乎是則六情之感先王爲之制其流而
未始拂之也四事之施先王爲之慎其感而未
始强之也此民心以和而樂之所自興也歟在
易有之天地感而萬物化生聖人感人心而天
punctuated: 者所當慎其動衆之原。志也，聲也，民之感於物而未化於物也，則有以養之：以禮道志，以樂和聲，所以培其本然之善者，其道蓋詳於上矣。行也，姦也，民之誘於物而將流於邪也，則有以閑之：以政一行，以刑防姦，所以禁其將萌之惡者，其道蓋豫於先矣。是禮與樂不一其事，而施之於民，則各神乎鼓舞之用；政與刑不同其道，而推之於下，則均妙乎化導之方。若此者何哉？蓋示之觀感以約其趨，善同好也，不善同惡也，會于其極而其心一焉，則不怨不爭，强弱之所以各安其分也，而道化於是乎宣布矣。納之範圍以聯其志，過思抑也，不及思企也，協于其中而其心一焉，則合愛合敬，智愚之所以各得其所也，而德教於是乎流行矣。民心旣同，治道不從是而出乎？是則六情之感，先王爲之制其流而未始拂之也；四事之施，先王爲之慎其感而未始强之也。此民心以和，而樂之所自興也歟？在《易》有之：「天地感而萬物化生，聖人感人心而天
translation_en: …was what required care on their part: the source of impulses that move the multitude. Intentions and sounds arise when the people are affected by things but have not yet been transformed by them; thus there are means to nurture them. Ritual guides intentions, and music harmonizes sounds. The means by which their innate goodness is cultivated have thus been fully provided by those above. Conduct and wrongdoing arise when the people are enticed by things and are about to stray into perversity; thus there are means to restrain them. Government unifies conduct, and punishments prevent wrongdoing. The means by which incipient evil is checked have thus been provided in advance. Ritual and music differ in their functions, yet when applied to the people, each works wondrously to inspire and stir them. Government and punishments differ in their methods, yet when extended to those below, both work marvelously as means of transforming and guiding them. Why is this so? By presenting examples that move people through observation, the former bring their inclinations into accord: all alike love what is good and hate what is not good. They converge upon the highest standard, and their hearts become one. Then there is neither resentment nor contention; strong and weak alike rest content in their respective stations, and the transforming influence of the Way spreads abroad. By bringing people within bounds, the latter unite their intentions: those who exceed the proper measure think of restraining themselves, and those who fall short think of reaching upward. They accord with the mean, and their hearts become one. Then they are united in love and respect; wise and foolish alike find their proper places, and moral instruction circulates throughout. Once the people's hearts are united, does not the way of good government proceed from this? Thus, when the six emotions were stirred, the former kings regulated their course without ever thwarting them. In applying these four instruments, the former kings took care over the responses they elicited without ever forcing them. Is this not how the people's hearts become harmonious and how music arises? The Book of Changes says: “Heaven and earth influence one another, and the myriad things are transformed and come into being; the sage influences people's hearts, and all under Heaven…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
下和平化生見天地之感和平見聖人之感其
致一也天下和平而樂其有不與乎樂書不言
律而言兵不言兵而言兵之用而言兵之偃嗚呼得之
矣安得知樂如太史公者而與之究作樂之本
第貳場
論
誠者聖人之本
張志皐
考試官教諭陳　批　體格正大議論精深非有
得於心學者不能道
===
考試官教授吳　批　此作究極本原是善發天
道聖人之藴者
論道者求諸從出之原則知聖人之同乎人而
非異乎人矣夫道之所從出者天也天以是道
賦於人無分於聖無分於愚也聖人亦即夫天
之所賦者全體而不虧焉非益之以理之所本
無也是故觀於實理流行之始聖人之所有夫
人之所必有也而不可謂之異觀於實理全體
punctuated:
下和平。化生見天地之感，和平見聖人之感，其致一也。天下和平，而樂其有不與乎？《樂書》不言律而言兵，不言兵而言兵之用，而言兵之偃。嗚呼，得之矣！安得知樂如太史公者，而與之究作樂之本？
第貳場
論
誠者聖人之本
張志皐
考試官教諭陳，批：體格正大，議論精深，非有得於心學者不能道。
考試官教授吳，批：此作究極本原，是善發天道聖人之藴者。
論道者求諸從出之原，則知聖人之同乎人而非異乎人矣。夫道之所從出者，天也。天以是道賦於人，無分於聖，無分於愚也。聖人亦即夫天之所賦者，全體而不虧焉，非益之以理之所本無也。是故觀於實理流行之始，聖人之所有，夫人之所必有也，而不可謂之異。觀於實理全體
translation_en:
…all under Heaven is peaceful and harmonious. Transformation and generation reveal the influence of Heaven and Earth; peace and harmony reveal the influence of the sage. Their ultimate effect is one. When all under Heaven is peaceful and harmonious, could music have no part in it? The Treatise on Music speaks not of pitch standards but of arms—not of arms themselves, but of their employment, and of their being laid aside. Ah, it has grasped the point! Where might one find someone who understands music as the Grand Historian did, with whom to investigate the foundations of making music?
Second Session
Discourse
“Sincerity Is the Foundation of the Sage”
Zhang Zhigao
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: Its form and style are upright and grand; its arguments are refined and profound. Only someone who has attained insight into the learning of the mind could express this.
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: This composition thoroughly investigates the ultimate source. It skillfully brings out the profound meanings of the Way of Heaven and of the sage.
If those who discuss the Way seek the source from which it proceeds, they will understand that the sage is the same as other people, rather than different from them. That from which the Way proceeds is Heaven. Heaven endows people with this Way, making no distinction between the sagely and the foolish. The sage simply preserves in its entirety, without impairment, what Heaven has bestowed; he does not augment it with anything that principle did not originally contain. Thus, viewed from the beginning of the flowing operation of real principle, what the sage possesses is what every person necessarily possesses, and he cannot be called different. Viewed in terms of the complete substance of real principle…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
訓誥本之深微而非高也退藏於密本之所以
翕聚也以彌六合本之所以流行也是故仁以
育天下本之形於慈愛也而生之不傷厚之不
困扶之不危者皆利賴於慈愛之本矣義以正
天下本之形於裁制也而以法相敘以信相考
以睦相守者皆利賴於裁制之本矣禮以節天
下本之形於度數也而品級有辨衣服有章井
牧有伍者皆利賴於度數之本矣智以察天下
本之形於昭晰也而明於吉凶洞乎利害審於
悔吝者皆利賴於昭晰之本矣以賛化育而天
有常覆地有常載者聖人之本爲之彌綸之也
以參天地而得一以清得一以寧者聖人之本
爲之範圍之也人見夫協和風動之治於唐虞
而不知欽明濬哲則堯舜之本爲之也人見夫
平成允懷之治於夏商而不知祗德建中則禹
湯之本爲之也人見夫咸和未清之治於有周
而不知徽柔敬義則文武之本爲之也究而論
之五帝以之官天下三王以之家天下禪繼不
punctuated: 訓誥，本之深微而非高也；退藏於密，本之所以翕聚也；以彌六合，本之所以流行也。是故仁以育天下，本之形於慈愛也，而生之不傷、厚之不困、扶之不危者，皆利賴於慈愛之本矣。義以正天下，本之形於裁制也，而以法相敘、以信相考、以睦相守者，皆利賴於裁制之本矣。禮以節天下，本之形於度數也，而品級有辨、衣服有章、井牧有伍者，皆利賴於度數之本矣。智以察天下，本之形於昭晰也，而明於吉凶、洞乎利害、審於悔吝者，皆利賴於昭晰之本矣。以賛化育，而天有常覆、地有常載者，聖人之本爲之彌綸之也；以參天地，而得一以清、得一以寧者，聖人之本爲之範圍之也。人見夫協和風動之治於唐虞，而不知欽明濬哲，則堯舜之本爲之也；人見夫平成允懷之治於夏商，而不知祗德建中，則禹湯之本爲之也；人見夫咸和未清之治於有周，而不知徽柔敬義，則文武之本爲之也。究而論之，五帝以之官天下，三王以之家天下，禪繼不
translation_en: … instructions and admonitions: the foundation is profound and subtle, yet not lofty. Withdrawing and concealing itself in secrecy is how the foundation gathers itself together; extending throughout the six directions is how it circulates. Thus, nurturing all under Heaven through benevolence is the foundation manifesting itself in compassionate love. Giving them life without injuring them, enriching them without distressing them, and supporting them without endangering them all depend for their benefit upon this foundation of compassionate love. Setting all under Heaven right through righteousness is the foundation manifesting itself in judgment and regulation. Ordering one another through laws, assessing one another through trustworthiness, and sustaining one another through concord all depend for their benefit upon this foundation of judgment and regulation. Regulating all under Heaven through ritual propriety is the foundation manifesting itself in measures and prescribed forms. Distinctions between ranks, prescribed patterns of dress, and the grouping of agricultural and pastoral lands all depend for their benefit upon this foundation of measures and prescribed forms. Discerning the affairs of all under Heaven through wisdom is the foundation manifesting itself in clarity. Understanding good and ill fortune, penetrating benefit and harm, and carefully discerning occasions for regret and shame all depend for their benefit upon this foundation of clarity. In assisting transformation and nurture, Heaven constantly covers and Earth constantly bears all things because the sage’s foundation comprehensively orders them. In forming a triad with Heaven and Earth, Heaven attains the One and thereby becomes clear, and Earth attains the One and thereby becomes tranquil, because the sage’s foundation provides their encompassing framework. People see the harmonious government of Tang and Yu, whose influence moved the people like the wind, but do not understand that reverent enlightenment and profound wisdom—the foundations of Yao and Shun—brought it about. People see the government of Xia and Shang, which brought order and accomplishment and won sincere allegiance, but do not understand that revering virtue and establishing the mean—the foundations of Yu and Tang—brought it about. People see the government of Zhou, in which all were harmonious and ‘not yet clear’ [?], but do not understand that gracious gentleness and reverent righteousness—the foundations of Kings Wen and Wu—brought it about. Examining the matter fully, the Five Emperors relied upon this to govern all under Heaven as a public charge, and the Three Kings relied upon it to govern all under Heaven as a hereditary possession. Abdication and hereditary succession did not …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
道憂治世享日中之豐者必嚴逸慾之防
故堯開衢室以咨賢舜闢總章而清問禹
下昌言之拜爰設鐸鞀武警怠勝之私載
銘户牖惟圖回乎至理故博採乎嘉猷迨
秦侈阿房漢靡長樂蘭林蕙草恣佚豫於
巡遊承露迎風椄羨門於䰟夢金馬以宏
達之大雅騁述作於篇章石渠以惇誨之
名儒競校讎於同異事浮華而鮮實制靡
麗以不經玆蓋伏遇
===
聖性夙成
睿謀神授
陶埏六籍
表正萬邦
仁被茅簷懷生咸樂于覆冒
化覃寰宇率土仰戴乎帡幪
崇政說書究義路禮門之旨
西嚮刈麥重播穀秉屋之風闢四門以納言
punctuated: 道憂治世，享日中之豐者，必嚴逸慾之防。故堯開衢室以咨賢，舜闢總章而清問，禹下昌言之拜，爰設鐸鞀；武警怠勝之私，載銘户牖。惟圖回乎至理，故博採乎嘉猷。迨秦侈阿房，漢靡長樂，蘭林蕙草，恣佚豫於巡遊；承露迎風，椄羨門於䰟夢。金馬以宏達之大雅，騁述作於篇章；石渠以惇誨之名儒，競校讎於同異。事浮華而鮮實，制靡麗以不經。玆蓋伏遇聖性夙成，睿謀神授，陶埏六籍，表正萬邦。仁被茅簷，懷生咸樂于覆冒；化覃寰宇，率土仰戴乎帡幪。崇政說書，究義路禮門之旨；西嚮刈麥，重播穀秉屋之風。闢四門以納言，
translation_en:
…the Way is concerned for an age of good government [?]. Those who enjoy the abundance of the sun at its zenith must strictly guard against ease and desire. Thus Yao opened the Hall of Thoroughfares to consult the worthy; Shun opened the Hall of General Assembly to solicit counsel; Yu bowed upon hearing excellent advice and established bells and drums for receiving remonstrance. King Wu guarded against the private inclination to let indolence prevail, inscribing admonitions on his doors and windows. Because they sought perfect governance, they gathered sound counsel widely.

Then Qin indulged in the extravagance of Epang Palace, and Han squandered resources on Changle Palace. Amid orchid groves and fragrant grasses, they gave free rein to pleasure on their tours. At the Dew-Receiving and Wind-Welcoming structures, they encountered the immortal Xianmen in their dreams [?]. At the Golden Horse Gate, learned and accomplished men of letters displayed their literary talents in compositions; at the Stone Conduit Pavilion, renowned Confucian scholars devoted to earnest instruction competed in collating textual agreements and discrepancies. Their undertakings were ostentatious but had little substance; their compositions were ornate but departed from the canonical norms.

Now, however, we humbly encounter Your Majesty, whose sagely nature matured early and whose discerning plans are divinely bestowed. You shape and mold through the Six Classics and set an upright example for the myriad states. Your benevolence reaches even thatched cottages, and all living beings rejoice beneath your shelter. Your transforming influence extends throughout the world, and all within the realm look up gratefully to your protection. At Chongzheng Hall, you hear the books expounded and investigate the meaning of righteousness as the road and ritual propriety as the gate. Facing west to reap wheat, you honor the tradition of sowing grain and “holding the house” [?]. You open the gates on all four sides to receive counsel…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
善無微而不錄舞兩階而格遠兵不用以
爲威廼者
臨朝訪道謂有羣彥之在前
燕處淸心欲授衆正而自助式營
二閣爰俾羣工筮龜恊以揆時土圭正而測
景據坤靈之正位抗應龍之虹梁離子督
繩玉瑱雕楹而璀璨奚斯削墨金璧飾璫
以熀煌蓬萊屹起乎中央采飾纖縟周廬
縈紆以外列朱文陸離虬負檐馬承阿狀
亭亭而干霧翬斯飛鳥斯革勢鍔鍔以翔
風規示建瓴占孚隆棟偉制獨裁於
宸斷鴻名渙發於
綸音謂英髦之在周行匪邇則疎何以資其
啓沃義理之關治道匪延則塞何以愽其
見聞旣取義以名居復垂情於鑒古無逸
圖上於孫奭忠㚖獻替之勤閣屛書成於
蔡襄爍若煙霞之麗曰中宗曰高宗曰祖
甲寅恭愼天命之嚴曰太王曰王季曰文
punctuated: 善無微而不錄，舞兩階而格遠，兵不用以爲威。廼者，臨朝訪道，謂有羣彥之在前；燕處淸心，欲授衆正而自助。式營二閣，爰俾羣工。筮龜恊以揆時，土圭正而測景。據坤靈之正位，抗應龍之虹梁。離子督繩，玉瑱雕楹而璀璨；奚斯削墨，金璧飾璫以熀煌。蓬萊屹起乎中央，采飾纖縟；周廬縈紆以外列，朱文陸離。虬負檐，馬承阿，狀亭亭而干霧；翬斯飛，鳥斯革，勢鍔鍔以翔風。規示建瓴，占孚隆棟。偉制獨裁於宸斷，鴻名渙發於綸音。謂英髦之在周行，匪邇則疎，何以資其啓沃？義理之關治道，匪延則塞，何以愽其見聞？旣取義以名居，復垂情於鑒古。無逸圖上於孫奭，忠㚖獻替之勤；閣屛書成於蔡襄，爍若煙霞之麗。曰中宗，曰高宗，曰祖甲，寅恭愼天命之嚴；曰太王，曰王季，曰文
translation_en: …no good deed, however small, goes unrecorded. By performing the dances between the two stairways, you bring distant peoples to submit; without employing arms, you establish your might. Recently, when attending court and inquiring into the Way, you wished to have a host of worthy men before you; when resting in private and clearing your mind, you wished to give upright men responsibilities so that they might assist you. Accordingly, you undertook the construction of two pavilions and charged the assembled craftsmen with the work. Milfoil and tortoise-shell divinations agreed in determining the proper time; the earth gnomon was correctly set to measure the sun’s shadow. Occupying the proper position upon the numinous earth, the buildings raise rainbow beams like winged dragons. Master Li [?] oversees the measuring cords; jade ornaments and carved pillars gleam. Xi Si trims the ink-marked timbers; gold and jade adorn the pendant ornaments with dazzling brilliance. Like Penglai, the central structure rises loftily, its colorful decorations delicate and elaborate. Surrounding lodges wind around its exterior, their vermilion patterns richly varied. Coiling dragons bear the eaves, and horses support the roof corners, their lofty forms reaching into the mist. Like pheasants in flight and birds spreading their wings, the buildings soar majestically upon the wind. Their design displays the commanding advantage of pouring water from a roof; the auspices confirm the promise of a lofty ridgepole. The magnificent design was determined solely by your imperial judgment; the grand names were proclaimed through your imperial words. You considered that, although outstanding men occupy the ranks of court, unless kept close they become estranged: how, then, could you draw upon their enlightening counsel? Moral principles bear upon the Way of governance, yet unless given fuller scope they become obstructed: how, then, could you broaden your knowledge? Having chosen meaningful names for these buildings, you further turned your attention to taking antiquity as a mirror. Sun Shi presented an Illustration of “Against Ease,” expressing loyal [?] diligence in advancing what was right and correcting what was wrong. Cai Xiang completed the calligraphy for the pavilion screen, radiant with the beauty of mist and rosy clouds. There are Zhongzong, Gaozong, and Zu Jia, reverently mindful of the stern Mandate of Heaven; there are King Tai, King Ji, and King Wen…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
王抑畏守卑服之儉璇題耀日繪稼穡小
入之依珠網羅星圖壽年享國之數絲毫
飛白並奎畫以騰輝銀榜抽黃儷天葩而
絢色出以觀入以省無勞披閱之煩寓於
目契於心庶獲對瞻之便臣等氣稟顓蒙
藝能迂拙才非閎博媿辟雍議禮之名思
則淹遲謝銅雀獻賦之敏螢窻夜習燭莫
莖於金蓮蓬戶陋居班豈知於玉筍周章
䖍列俯仰懷慙鄭璞齊竽濫荷鹽梅之寄
===
秦冠漢綬曷光夢卜之求代言非陸贄之
工疇能助發揮於睿藻識書乏安世之學
何以備顧問於禁林然敢不勉竭葵忱用
酬
乾造戒流連於圖內効班伯之讜論臣時可
奏事於帳中希汲黯之直言悟主所其無
逸時進逆耳之規能自得師務期永命之
道伏願
不邇不殖正心洞啓乎重門
punctuated: 王，抑畏守卑服之儉。璇題耀日，繪稼穡小入之依；珠網羅星，圖壽年享國之數。絲毫飛白，並奎畫以騰輝；銀榜抽黃，儷天葩而絢色。出以觀，入以省，無勞披閱之煩；寓於目，契於心，庶獲對瞻之便。臣等氣稟顓蒙，藝能迂拙，才非閎博，媿辟雍議禮之名；思則淹遲，謝銅雀獻賦之敏。螢窻夜習，燭莫莖於金蓮；蓬戶陋居，班豈知於玉筍。周章䖍列，俯仰懷慙。鄭璞齊竽，濫荷鹽梅之寄；秦冠漢綬，曷光夢卜之求？代言非陸贄之工，疇能助發揮於睿藻？識書乏安世之學，何以備顧問於禁林？然敢不勉竭葵忱，用酬乾造？戒流連於圖內，効班伯之讜論臣時可；奏事於帳中，希汲黯之直言悟主。所其無逸，時進逆耳之規；能自得師，務期永命之道。伏願：不邇不殖，正心洞啓乎重門。
translation_en:
…King Wen: reverent and fearful, they maintained frugality in humble clothing. The jeweled headings shine in the sun, depicting farming as the common people's support [?]; the pearl mesh arrays the stars, charting the numbers of years they lived and ruled. Fine brushstrokes in the “flying-white” style shine alongside Your Majesty's calligraphy; silver tablets and yellow lettering [?] display brilliant colors beside heavenly blossoms. Going out, one may contemplate them; coming in, one may reflect upon them, without the trouble of opening and reading a volume. Set before the eyes and understood in the heart, they may thus offer the convenience of direct contemplation.

We, your servants, are obtuse and ignorant by disposition, and our abilities are unpolished and inept. Our talents lack breadth, and we are ashamed to bear the reputation of those who discussed ritual in the Biyong ceremonial academy. Our thoughts come slowly, and we cannot match the quickness of those who presented rhapsodies at the Bronze Sparrow Terrace. Studying at night by a firefly-lit window, we have no golden-lotus candles [?]; dwelling in humble homes with brushwood doors, how could we know the court ranks arrayed like jade bamboo shoots? Anxiously taking our places in reverence, we feel shame whether looking down or up. Like the supposed uncut jade of Zheng and the unskilled reed-organ player of Qi, we have undeservedly received the charge of serving as salt and plum to season government. Wearing Qin caps and Han seals and ribbons, how could we bring glory to the search for worthy ministers through dreams and divination?

In drafting pronouncements, we lack Lu Zhi's skill: who among us could help give expression to Your Majesty's elegant compositions? In knowledge of writings, we lack Zhang Anshi's learning: how could we stand ready for consultation in the Hanlin Academy? Yet how dare we fail to exert ourselves fully in sunflower-like devotion, to repay Your Majesty's nurturing grace? In warning against lingering over the images, we would emulate Ban Bo's forthright remonstrance [the following words, 臣時可, are unclear]; in presenting affairs within the curtained chamber, we aspire to Ji An's plain speaking that brought understanding to his ruler. Taking freedom from ease as one's abiding principle, we would regularly offer admonitions unwelcome to the ear; that Your Majesty may find a teacher for himself, we would strive for the Way that perpetuates Heaven's mandate.

We humbly pray: draw not near to things of pleasure, nor increase them; rectify your heart, opening wide the successive gates…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
惟一惟精主靜常惺於虛室
蓋如天而容如地仁恩逮於向隅
言必聽而諫必行虛受通乎自牖
盛德大業建
皇極於無疆
景福殊祥鞏
國祚於有永臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
===
表稱
賀以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
陸宗龍
考試官教諭陳 批 能掄揚我
皇上文武之烈而知本要所在亦涵泳
punctuated:
惟一惟精，主靜常惺於虛室；蓋如天而容如地，仁恩逮於向隅；言必聽而諫必行，虛受通乎自牖。盛德大業，建皇極於無疆；景福殊祥，鞏國祚於有永。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
陸宗龍
考試官教諭陳批：「能掄揚我皇上文武之烈，而知本要所在，亦涵泳」
translation_en:
…May you remain single-minded and refined in purpose, maintaining stillness and constant awareness in the empty chamber of the mind. May you shelter like Heaven and embrace like Earth, extending benevolence and favor even to those left facing the corner. May you invariably heed counsel and act upon remonstrance, receiving advice with an open mind, accessible as through a window. Through abundant virtue and great achievements, establish the sovereign standard without limit; through great blessings and exceptional auspicious signs, secure the dynasty’s fortunes forever. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty, overcome with fervent emotion and trembling awe.
