Reckoned together, a year's receipts do not suffice for a year's expenditure. How, under such circumstances, can sudden emergencies be met? Only by making regular inspection tours to supervise tax collection and maintaining personal integrity so as to treat the people generously will they willingly remit their land taxes and the reserves remain consistently full. Some argue that, in terms of their own interests, Sichuan and Huguang are securing the gateways to their two provinces; in terms of their greater duty, they are jointly defending the court's frontiers. Surely this was the original intention behind establishing the system?
Postal relay service is assessed upon the civilian population by quota, but performed in their stead by soldiers—a system already different from that of the central provinces. At first, expenditure was still modest. Now, however, envoys from three provinces travel through, and expenses are multiplied by demands and exactions [?], so the system has become thoroughly exhausted. If the service is left to the civilians, they flee deep into the forests and bamboo thickets; if it is imposed upon the soldiers, they already cannot bear burdens beyond their quotas. Under the old regulations, Yunnan provides silver as a subsidy, but it does not suffice for the onerous demands of provisioning. If indeed …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
使冗票必革不以徇夫濫借之差需索必
懲不以寛諸生事之輩庶驛傳之倒懸解
矣而軍可也民亦可也又何俟於滇省之
歲遺乎站堡之伍不以城守而以之迎送
制已殊乎中土矣初猶宦轍之稀也今則
行李之往來山徑之負戴蓋雜然煩矣輕
者間日一差重者月無虛日往歲督撫有
限扛之議然條約之示罔聞也誠使募其
少壯塡夫空乏之伍均其多寡濟以通融
===
之法庶站堡之奔命蘇矣而增糧之議亦
無見於課有定額也夫豈折衷之定論乎
民資於田田資於水也貴之崇岡挿天隴
畝列焉並藉夫天澤之濡耳浹旬不雨民
且狼狽而公家之賦不輸矣然陂堰之疏
築有方則天時之旱澇有備如史起引漳
水以漑鄴而舃鹵稻粱之詠至今膾炙人
口也不可倣而行之乎民有華夷性無間
於華夷也貴之黌序並與弟子充焉咸利
punctuated:
使冗票必革，不以徇夫濫借之差；需索必懲，不以寛諸生事之輩，庶驛傳之倒懸解矣。而軍可也，民亦可也，又何俟於滇省之歲遺乎？站堡之伍，不以城守，而以之迎送，制已殊乎中土矣。初猶宦轍之稀也，今則行李之往來，山徑之負戴，蓋雜然煩矣。輕者間日一差，重者月無虛日。往歲督撫有限扛之議，然條約之示罔聞也。誠使募其少壯，塡夫空乏之伍，均其多寡，濟以通融之法，庶站堡之奔命蘇矣。而增糧之議，亦無見於課有定額也，夫豈折衷之定論乎？

民資於田，田資於水也。貴之崇岡挿天，隴畝列焉，並藉夫天澤之濡耳。浹旬不雨，民且狼狽，而公家之賦不輸矣。然陂堰之疏築有方，則天時之旱澇有備。如史起引漳水以漑鄴，而舃鹵稻粱之詠，至今膾炙人口也，不可倣而行之乎？民有華夷，性無間於華夷也。貴之黌序，並與弟子充焉，咸利
translation_en:
…if superfluous service warrants were invariably abolished, without indulging those who improperly invoke official assignments, and extortionate demands invariably punished, without leniency toward troublemakers, the desperate plight of the postal relay service might be relieved. This would serve both soldiers and civilians: why then wait for the annual subsidy from Yunnan?

The personnel of relay stations and forts are employed not in defending their posts but in receiving and escorting travelers—a system already unlike that of the central provinces. At first, official travelers were relatively few; now the passage of travelers and the carrying of burdens along mountain paths have become a complicated and onerous business. Those lightly burdened are assigned service every other day; those heavily burdened have not a single free day in the month. In past years, the supreme commander and provincial governor proposed limits on porter service, yet nothing has been heard of regulations being promulgated. If young, able-bodied men were recruited to fill depleted units, personnel numbers equalized, and flexible arrangements used to make up deficiencies, the exhausting demands upon the stations and forts might be alleviated. Yet proposals to increase grain allowances also fail to recognize that tax assessments have fixed quotas [?]. Could this be considered a definitive, balanced judgment?

The people depend upon fields, and fields depend upon water. In Guizhou, lofty ridges pierce the sky, with cultivated plots arrayed upon them, all relying upon rain from heaven for moisture. If no rain falls for ten days, the people are already in distress and cannot pay the public taxes. But if ponds and weirs are properly dredged and constructed, provision can be made against both drought and flooding. Shi Qi, for example, diverted the Zhang River to irrigate Ye; the song about saline land yielding rice and millet remains on everyone’s lips to this day. Could his example not be followed?

Among the people there are both Hua and Yi, but human nature does not differ between Hua and Yi. Guizhou’s schools, too, are filled with pupils; all the benefits…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
夫占籍之流耳諸酋之子不得在列而獷
戾之性自若矣然禮義之化導既至則蠻
貊之忠信可行如常袞明敎化以率民而
曼胡青衿之効至今爛然史策也不可倣
而行之乎事不統於一則令泥難行今湖
之衛所錯列於鎮仁之墟川之府司分據
於思銅之境在彼爲僻壤既阻於撫綏之
不逮在我爲要區又病於控轄之不專以
勾攝則梗令而姦宄之訊詰爲艱以徵呼
===
則亡命而稅糧之逋負日積在昔守臣有
割平清偏鎭之疏諸司有割永播烏芒之
議豈非經遠之猷而今日之所當申請者
乎化不必於更則患滋難彌今土司之大
者逞衆橫行而蠶食無已小者乘機竊發
而侵掠不休骨肉相殘安然不覺其非父
子就戮恬然不知所畏興師問罪率遠遯
以自全移文督責又空言而無補即其一
時强梗之迹雖殄滅而郡縣之豈曰不宜
punctuated: 夫占籍之流耳。諸酋之子不得在列，而獷戾之性自若矣。然禮義之化導既至，則蠻貊之忠信可行。如常袞明敎化以率民，而曼胡青衿之効，至今爛然史策也，不可倣而行之乎？事不統於一，則令泥難行。今湖之衛所錯列於鎮仁之墟，川之府司分據於思銅之境。在彼爲僻壤，既阻於撫綏之不逮；在我爲要區，又病於控轄之不專。以勾攝，則梗令而姦宄之訊詰爲艱；以徵呼，則亡命而稅糧之逋負日積。在昔守臣有割平清偏鎭之疏，諸司有割永播烏芒之議，豈非經遠之猷，而今日之所當申請者乎？化不必於更，則患滋難彌。今土司之大者逞衆橫行，而蠶食無已；小者乘機竊發，而侵掠不休。骨肉相殘，安然不覺其非；父子就戮，恬然不知所畏。興師問罪，率遠遯以自全；移文督責，又空言而無補。即其一時强梗之迹，雖殄滅而郡縣之，豈曰不宜？
translation_en:
…those who have registered locally, and no others. The sons of the various chieftains cannot be included among them, and their fierce and unruly dispositions remain unchanged. Yet once instruction in ritual propriety and righteousness has fully reached them, loyalty and trustworthiness can be practiced even among the Man and Mo peoples. For example, Chang Gun led the people by promoting moral instruction, with the result that those wearing broad barbarian collars donned the blue collars of students. This achievement still shines brilliantly in the historical records. Could it not be emulated and put into practice?

When affairs are not unified under a single authority, orders become obstructed and difficult to enforce. At present, guards and battalions belonging to Huguang are interspersed throughout the lands of Zhen and Ren, while prefectures and native offices belonging to Sichuan occupy separate portions of the territory of Si and Tong. To those provinces these are remote lands, hindered by the failure of their pacification efforts to reach them; to us they are vital areas, yet they suffer from the lack of exclusive jurisdiction. When arrests are ordered, commands are obstructed, making it difficult to interrogate criminals; when demands for payment are issued, people flee, and arrears in tax grain accumulate daily. In former times, regional officials submitted memorials proposing the transfer of Ping, Qing, Pian, and Zhen, and the various offices discussed transferring Yong, Bo, Wu, and Mang. Were these not far-sighted plans, for which petitions ought to be submitted today?

If reform is not carried through by changing existing arrangements [?], troubles multiply and become difficult to put an end to. At present, the larger native chieftaincies rely on their numbers to act lawlessly, encroaching without end; the smaller ones seize opportunities to launch sudden attacks, invading and plundering without respite. Close relatives slaughter one another, calmly unaware that they are doing wrong; fathers and sons face execution, yet remain untroubled and know no fear. When troops are raised to call them to account, they generally flee far away to preserve themselves; when official communications are sent to admonish and reprimand them, these too are empty words that accomplish nothing. Considering their acts of defiance at a given time, even if they were exterminated and their territories constituted as prefectures and counties, how could this be called inappropriate? …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
念其先世歸服之忱仍化誨而懷服之未
或不可豈非彌患之策而今日之所當叅
酌者乎夫天下一家也必其綜理得人而
後一家之事無不理若任其縱橫而漫無
統紀其不至於決裂者幾希天下一身也
必其血氣周流而後一身之養無不周若
隨其耗竭而不知節宣其不至於危亡者
幾希嗟夫今貴陽之事何以異此兵不足
以實伍也司兵者貴有優恤之方糧不足
===
以充餉也司計者貴得催科之善驛傳懲
騷擾之姦則館役樂於趨事站堡酌均平
之則則疲伍幸於息肩司牧者史起其人
則灌溉之利溥而田皆沃壤矣司教者常
衮其人則椎結之習變而人皆冠裳矣盡
一之議定則規制善而治有裨於邊疆化
誨之令行則悔悟興而患或彌於旦夕譬
之理家者有綜理之術無決裂之憂善理
家者也理身者有保衛之方無耗竭之害
punctuated:
念其先世歸服之忱，仍化誨而懷服之，未或不可，豈非彌患之策，而今日之所當叅酌者乎？夫天下一家也，必其綜理得人，而後一家之事無不理；若任其縱橫，而漫無統紀，其不至於決裂者幾希。天下一身也，必其血氣周流，而後一身之養無不周；若隨其耗竭，而不知節宣，其不至於危亡者幾希。
嗟夫！今貴陽之事，何以異此？兵不足以實伍也，司兵者貴有優恤之方；糧不足以充餉也，司計者貴得催科之善。驛傳懲騷擾之姦，則館役樂於趨事；站堡酌均平之則，則疲伍幸於息肩。司牧者史起其人，則灌溉之利溥，而田皆沃壤矣；司教者常衮其人，則椎結之習變，而人皆冠裳矣。盡一之議定，則規制善，而治有裨於邊疆；化誨之令行，則悔悟興，而患或彌於旦夕。譬之理家者，有綜理之術，無決裂之憂，善理家者也；理身者，有保衛之方，無耗竭之害
translation_en:
…Considering the sincerity with which their ancestors submitted to our rule, it might still be possible to instruct and transform them, winning their allegiance through benevolent care. Would this not be a strategy for ending trouble, and one that ought to be weighed today? All under Heaven is one household: only when the right people oversee its affairs will everything in that household be properly managed. If people are allowed to act without restraint, with no overarching order, there is little chance of avoiding disintegration. All under Heaven is one body: only when its blood and vital energy circulate throughout will every part receive nourishment. If these are allowed to become exhausted, with no understanding of how to regulate their expenditure and circulation, there is little chance of avoiding peril and destruction.
Alas! How do present affairs in Guiyang differ from this? When there are too few soldiers to fill the ranks, those responsible for military affairs must have ways to provide them generous care and relief. When grain is insufficient for military provisions, those responsible for finances must collect taxes effectively. If abuses that harass the people are punished in the postal relay service, the relay-hostel workers will gladly attend to their duties. If equitable rules are worked out for relay stations and forts, weary soldiers will be fortunate enough to lay down their burdens. If those who govern the people are men like Shi Qi, the benefits of irrigation will spread widely, and all fields will become fertile soil. If those responsible for education are men like Chang Gun, the custom of wearing club-shaped topknots will change, and all will wear the caps and robes of civilized society. Once the proposal for unification [?] is settled, institutions will be sound, and government will benefit the frontier. Once orders for moral instruction are implemented, repentance and understanding will arise, and trouble may be quelled within a day. To draw an analogy with managing a household: someone who has methods for overseeing its affairs and no fear of disintegration manages a household well. Someone who tends the body, possessing ways to safeguard it and suffering no harm from exhaustion…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
善理身者也愚生竊伏荒陬晷與經國之
遠猷而目擊時艱扼腕而展轉於懷者亦
有年矣狂瞽之見幸承明問以復惟試聽
而終教之
punctuated: 善理身者也。愚生竊伏荒陬，晷與經國之遠猷，而目擊時艱，扼腕而展轉於懷者亦有年矣。狂瞽之見，幸承明問以復，惟試聽而終教之。
translation_en: …such a person is skilled at caring for his own body. I, an unworthy scholar, dwell obscurely in a remote corner, with little part in far-reaching plans for governing the realm [?]. Yet I have witnessed the difficulties of the times, and for years have wrung my hands in distress as these concerns turn over and over in my mind. These rash and unenlightened views I offer in reply to the discerning question I have been fortunate to receive. I ask that you give them a hearing and complete my instruction.

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
貴州鄉試錄後序
歲維庚午大比黔士報成爲
賢書以
獻彬職當有言迺晉多士申告
之曰谷爾多士蔚乎文哉
邦家之光也奚翅光于黔乎哉
夫黔昔在荒服之外其俗喬
===
而野樸而不文狉狉然夷也
今濟濟乎彬彬乎卽中州莫
踰焉是
聖天子文教之漸被薄海內外罔
不率俾以臻于此猗與休哉
彬始至黔竊計黔士之選止
三十人爾殫厥心以圖之可
punctuated:
貴州鄉試錄後序

歲維庚午，大比黔士，報成爲賢書以獻。彬職當有言，迺晉多士，申告之曰：「谷爾多士，蔚乎文哉！邦家之光也，奚翅光于黔乎哉！夫黔昔在荒服之外，其俗喬而野，樸而不文，狉狉然夷也。今濟濟乎，彬彬乎，卽中州莫踰焉。是聖天子文教之漸被，薄海內外罔不率俾，以臻于此。猗與休哉！」

彬始至黔，竊計黔士之選止三十人爾，殫厥心以圖之，可
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guizhou Provincial Examination

In the gengwu year [1570], the scholars of Qian [Guizhou] underwent the triennial examination. Upon its completion, the results were compiled into a register of worthy men for presentation to the throne. I, Bin, was obliged by my office to offer some words. Accordingly, I called the assembled scholars forward and addressed them: “You worthy scholars [?], how splendid is your literary accomplishment! You bring glory to the realm: how could that glory be confined to Qian alone? In former times, Qian lay beyond even the outermost zone of imperial dominion. Its customs were unruly and rustic, simple and unrefined; its people lived as uncultivated tribes. Now, how dignified and accomplished they are! Even the central provinces cannot surpass them. This is the gradual, far-reaching influence of our sagely Son of Heaven’s civilizing instruction. Throughout the lands bounded by the seas and beyond, none fail to follow and submit, thus bringing about this achievement. Ah, how glorious!”

When I, Bin, first arrived in Qian, I reflected privately that only thirty men were to be selected from among its scholars. If I devoted all my care to planning the selection, it would be possible…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
使無遺賢已及縱觀其文而
讎校之言人人殊咸不詭于
道炳耀焜煌悅心而炫目比
比是已眞賢良在玆乎盜盡
于玆無遺乎而數止于三十
額限之已將若之何旣而思
之亦旣殫厥心矣苟有一名
===
世者出于其間以佐成
聖天子文德之敷其爲
邦家之光不旣大乎奚以多爲
虞臣以五周臣以十振古得
賢之盛莫與媲美矧黔之選
於周三之於虞六之不旣多
乎比屋可以班瑞罝兔可以
punctuated: 使無遺賢已。及縱觀其文而讎校之，言人人殊，咸不詭于道，炳耀焜煌，悅心而炫目，比比是已。眞賢良在玆乎？盜盡于玆無遺乎？而數止于三十，額限之已，將若之何？旣而思之，亦旣殫厥心矣。苟有一名世者出于其間，以佐成聖天子文德之敷，其爲邦家之光，不旣大乎？奚以多爲？虞臣以五，周臣以十，振古得賢之盛，莫與媲美。矧黔之選，於周三之，於虞六之，不旣多乎？比屋可以班瑞，罝兔可以
translation_en:
…ensure that no worthy man was overlooked. Yet when I surveyed their writings and compared and assessed them, each man expressed himself differently, but none departed from the Way. Brilliant and radiant, pleasing the heart and dazzling the eyes—such writings were everywhere. Are the truly worthy and good all here? Are they all gathered here, with none left out [?]? Yet the number is restricted to thirty: the quota sets this limit. What can be done? On further reflection, I had already devoted my utmost efforts to the task. If even one man renowned in his age should emerge from among them to help spread the sage Son of Heaven’s civil virtue, would he not bring great glory to the state? Why seek large numbers?

The sovereign of Yu had five ministers, and Zhou had ten. Throughout antiquity, no flourishing age of recruiting worthy men could rival these. Moreover, Guizhou’s selection numbers three times that of Zhou and six times that of Yu. Is this not already many? Household after household could receive jade insignia of rank, and those who set nets for rabbits could …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
干城虞周之治固如此也士
毋謂黔而少之諸有司有厚
望焉雖然文治之盛黔于今
蔑以加已文之盛質之漓也
盍毋思其敝乎敝乎周曰
郁郁乎文哉故從周懼其文
之盛其敝也至于不慚故又
===
曰從先進先進失之野奚從
焉從其質也梂文之敝莫如
質與其不慚也盍野以質之
尚存焉耳子欲居九夷其從
先進之心乎今黔非昔黔已
其文之始盛質之始漓乎識
之早返之易爾語曰旣彫旣
punctuated: 干城，虞周之治固如此也。士毋謂黔而少之，諸有司有厚望焉。雖然，文治之盛，黔于今蔑以加已。文之盛，質之漓也，盍毋思其敝乎？敝乎周，曰：「郁郁乎文哉！」故從周。懼其文之盛，其敝也至于不慚，故又曰：「從先進。」先進失之野，奚從焉？從其質也。梂文之敝，莫如質。與其不慚也，盍野，以質之尚存焉耳。子欲居九夷，其從先進之心乎？今黔非昔黔已，其文之始盛，質之始漓乎？識之早，返之易爾。語曰：「旣彫旣
translation_en: …serve as shields and walls: such indeed was government under Yu and Zhou. Scholars should not disparage these men because they come from Qian. The officials have great hopes for them. Nevertheless, the flourishing of civil culture in Qian today could scarcely be surpassed. Yet as cultural refinement flourishes, native substance grows thin. Should we not consider the resulting abuses? These abuses appeared in Zhou [?]. Confucius said, “How splendid its culture!” Thus he followed Zhou. Fearing that excessive refinement would degenerate into shamelessness, however, he also said, “I follow the men of earlier times.” If those earlier men erred on the side of rusticity, why follow them? It was their native substance that he followed. To remedy [?] the abuses of refinement, nothing is better than substance. Rather than be shameless, why not be rustic, since native substance at least remains therein? When the Master wished to live among the Nine Yi peoples, was this not the same disposition that led him to follow the men of earlier times? Qian today is no longer the Qian of old. Is its refinement beginning to flourish while its substance begins to grow thin? Recognize this early, and returning will be easy. As the saying goes, “Once carved, once …

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
琢還乎其樸爾多士念之哉
毋不㪿于文而忘其質毋飾
先資以徼榮而忘名世之實
毋飾詐以怙寵以貽有司不
適之謫毋身便是圖以負
主上寤寐求賢之急尚念之哉頃
者蕞夷冥頑梗化
===
聖天子用師於黔廼于黔士之選
亟汲汲焉不可以觀
上意所嚮歟昔在帝虞有苗弗率
命禹徂征益賛之曰惟德動
天無遠不届舜乃誕敷文德
舞干羽于兩階有苗來格今
選士以文矢文德也鉛槧之
punctuated:
琢，還乎其樸。」爾多士念之哉！毋不㪿于文而忘其質，毋飾先資以徼榮而忘名世之實，毋飾詐以怙寵，以貽有司不適之謫，毋身便是圖，以負主上寤寐求賢之急。尚念之哉！
頃者，蕞夷冥頑梗化，聖天子用師於黔，廼于黔士之選亟汲汲焉，不可以觀上意所嚮歟？昔在帝虞，有苗弗率，命禹徂征。益賛之曰：「惟德動天，無遠不届。」舜乃誕敷文德，舞干羽于兩階，有苗來格。今選士以文，矢文德也。鉛槧之
translation_en:
…polished, return to original simplicity.” You scholars, ponder this! Do not become wholly bent upon literary refinement [?] and forget its underlying substance. Do not embellish your prior qualifications [?] to seek glory and forget the genuine accomplishments that make a name in your age. Do not dress up deceit to secure favor, thereby bringing upon the responsible officials the reproach of having selected unsuitable men. Do not pursue only your own convenience, disappointing His Majesty’s urgent quest for worthy men, which occupies him waking and sleeping. Do give this thought!
Recently, the petty tribes, benighted and obstinate, resisted transformation, and the sagely Son of Heaven employed troops in Guizhou. Yet he has been most urgently concerned with selecting scholars from Guizhou. Does this not reveal the direction of His Majesty’s intentions? Formerly, under the sovereign of Yu, the Miao would not obey, and he commanded Yu to march against them. Yi encouraged him, saying: “Only virtue moves Heaven; no place is too distant for it to reach.” Shun then spread civil virtue far and wide and had dances with shields and feather plumes performed between the two stairways; the Miao came and submitted. Now, selecting scholars through literary accomplishment manifests civil virtue. The lead stylus and wooden writing tablet’s…

title: 隆慶四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
操其干羽之舞乎籲俊以尊
帝
天且格之矧茲有苗爾多士尚以
虞周之俊是期乎故敢于末
簡猷告于爾多士以終文德
之義云
江西饒州府餘干縣儒學教
===
諭陳彬謹序
punctuated:
操，其干羽之舞乎？籲俊以尊帝，天且格之，矧茲有苗！爾多士尚以虞周之俊是期乎？故敢于末簡猷告于爾多士，以終文德之義云。
江西饒州府餘干縣儒學教諭陳彬謹序。
translation_en:
…the practice of writing: is this not the dance with shields and plumes? Worthy men are summoned to honor the emperor; even Heaven can be moved by this, how much more these Miao! You assembled scholars, will you not aspire to match the worthies of Yu and Zhou? Thus, on these final leaves, I venture to address you scholars with these counsels, concluding my account of the significance of civil virtue.
Preface respectfully composed by Chen Bin, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yugan County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.
